### Addendum 125: two blueprints for the Birkhoff form (`UniformConvergence/`), and what the source hides

Instruction (verbatim): *"We will improve this to the form needed in the directory IET2, see the file
ChallengeWeak.lean where the form we will be after is called MasurVeechFun … The new files will be part
of the project MasurVeech, in a subdirectory UniformConvergence. For this, we need two tools: (1) if a
homeomorphism of a nonempty compact space is uniquely ergodic, then the Birkhoff averages of continuous
functions converge uniformly to the average. (2) extending (1) to interval exchange transformations,
which are not continuous. You will write two detailed mathematical blueprints for these two tools …
on the top of page 55. The writing is quite terse here, so you will expand greatly the arguments."*

**No `.lean` file was touched, so there is no build to report.** What was produced is documentation:
the Birkhoff campaign's three documents (352 + 895 + 93 lines). The
Lean sources of the next round are planned as `UniformConvergence/*.lean`. The
existing README line "the Birkhoff-averages form is not formalised here" (`README.md:67` of that project)
and the deferred item D1 of `blueprint.md:853` are what this round is about.

**Tool 1** is the standard theorem (Oxtoby/Walters), proved in full, plus the *relative form* that
Tool 2 actually consumes: it suffices that every invariant probability measure supported on the closure
of the set of initial points gives the same integral. Minimality and invertibility are never used.
Mathlib already has everything except the assembly: `instCompactSpaceProbabilityMeasure`,
`tendsto_iff_forall_integral_tendsto`, `birkhoffAverage`, `ext_of_forall_integral_eq_of_IsFiniteMeasure`.

**Tool 2 — three corrections to the source paragraph, all recorded in Blueprint 2 §8.**

1. *"`T̃` is easily seen to be uniquely ergodic"* is **false**: `L a = a`, so the left germ of the left
   endpoint is a fixed point of `T̃` for every exchange (and it is isolated). The replacement is a
   transfer statement: with `ρ = proj_*ν` and `J` the finite jump set,
   `∫g dρ − ∫g d(T_*ρ) = Σ_{c∈J} ν{leftGerm c}(g(Lc) − g(Tc))`, and "mass is constant along a
   `T̃`-orbit" kills the defect *provided* (H2) below. The lift of `λ` is then unique because `proj` is
   injective off the countable split set and `λ` has no atoms (this is where atomlessness enters — the
   same point `blueprint.md:634` predicted for D1).
2. **(H2) = "the left-limit map `L` has no periodic point in `(a,b]`" is necessary, not cosmetic.** If
   `x₀ ∈ (a,b)` is `L`-periodic of period `k`, the maps `A_n = (1/n)Σ_{i<n}ψ ∘ p ∘ T̃^[i]` are continuous
   on the split space, `A_n(leftGerm x₀) → (1/k)Σ_j ψ x_j`, and `leftGerm x₀` is a limit of right germs;
   uniform convergence would force `(1/k)Σ_j δ_{x_j} = λ`, impossible. So the *pointwise* theorem needs
   (H2); the a.e. statement does not, because (H2) fails only on a countable union of hyperplanes.
3. *No* compactification carries a homeomorphism `T̃` with `p ∘ T̃ = T ∘ p` everywhere: at a cut `c` a
   net `y ↑ c` converges to the left germ of `c` while `T y → L c ≠ T c`. `T̃` is the **germ map**
   (right germs ↦ right germs of `T x`, left germs ↦ left germs of `L x`), and the semi-conjugacy holds
   on right germs only — which is all that is used. The split set must be the full orbit closure
   `⋃_{n∈ℤ}T^n(s ∪ s' ∪ {b})`: the source's one-sided unions coincide with it (`T s ⊆ s'`,
   `T⁻¹ s' ⊆ s`), but `{b}` has to be added (`b` is a left discontinuity).

The construction avoids the order topology: the space is a closed subspace of
`[a,b] × {false,true}^D`, which gives compact, Hausdorff, pseudo-metrizable and Borel from instances,
and continuity of `T̃` becomes a two-coordinate case analysis.

**Lemma 6.2, the one open point of the first version, is now proved.** It said: for `π` irreducible and
`0 ≠ m ≥ 0`, the functional `λ ↦ Σ_α m_α δ_α(λ)` is not identically zero (equivalently
`ker Ω^t ∩ ℝ_{≥0}^d = {0}`), which is what makes the exceptional set of (H2) a countable union of
*proper* hyperplanes. Proved in the round `.ultramath/smvz4odkr` (member `m3`, accepted; the three other
members were stopped): `c(m)_β = m(I_β) − m(π⁻¹(I_{πβ}))`, and if this vanishes with `m ≥ 0 ≠ 0`, the
least support element `f` satisfies `π f = min π(supp m)` (test (T) at `β = f`), then
`{β : πβ < πf} = I_{f−1}` (both directions from (T)), so cardinalities give `π f = f` and
`π(I_{f−1}) = I_{f−1}` — a proper invariant initial segment, against irreducibility; `f = 0` gives
`π 0 = 0`. Sharp form: for *arbitrary* `π`, a non-negative kernel vector exists iff there is such an
`f`, the converse being `m = e_f`. Real (not just integral) `m`, and `d ≥ 2` is used exactly at `f = 0`.

**Verification of that proof** (referee's own, independent of the member's scripts): the identity for
4000 random *signed rational* instances with `d ≤ 9`; the Lemma's full conclusion on all 4091 cases
with `c(m) = 0` for `d ≤ 6` including reducible `π`; Statement A exhaustively over irreducible `π` for
`(d,K) = (2,4),(3,4),(4,3),(5,3),(6,2)`; the sharp form over all `π` with `d ≤ 7`; 3000 random rational
trials. Zero failures throughout (`/tmp`-free: `.scratch/ref_swarm.py`, plus the member's
`.ultramath/smvz4odkr/m3/verify*.py`, which run clean).

**Open decisions, for the author.** (i) `UniqueErgodicFun`/`MasurVeechFun` are declared in
`IET2/ChallengeWeak.lean` against the `IET2/IETFree` copies; the plan copies both declarations verbatim
into `UniformConvergence/Basic.lean` of that project and proves `MasurVeechFun` there, `IET2` then copying
them or depending on it. (ii) Whether (H2) stays an explicit hypothesis of the pointwise
theorem (it is invisible in the a.e. form), or is to be replaced by "no connection".

### Addendum 126: (H2) is a theorem — a periodic left limit is a periodic interval

Instruction (verbatim): *"(H2) should not be needed: if an IET is uniquely ergodic, then it is
minimal, and then by Keane's condition it has no connection. Don't start on the formalization yet.
Instead, investigate if you agree with my argument. If you do, integrate it to the blueprint,
together with the proof of Keane's theorem that no connections is equivalent to minimality. A proof
of this is included in Yoccoz's notes."*

**Verdict: the conclusion is right, the argument is not, and there is a better argument.** No
`.lean` file touched; Blueprint 2 rewritten (§4.4 new, §5 unconditional, §6 demoted to an appendix,
§8.6 new, §9–§11 adjusted), README updated.

**Why the stated chain fails.** Keane's theorem is *not* an equivalence. Yoccoz, article p. 17
(PDF p. 30): Theorem 5.9 *(Keane) "If an i.e.m. has no connection, it is minimal"*, and immediately
below it Exercise 5.11: *"For d = 2, T is minimal iff there is no connection … For d ≥ 3, show that
there exists T minimal but having a connection, and also T with no connection but lengths data
rationally dependent."* So `minimal ⇒ no connection` is **false for d ≥ 3**, which is exactly the
range of `MasurVeechFun`; the argument uses Keane's theorem in the direction it does not have. The
first step (`uniquely ergodic ⇒ minimal`) is presumably true but its proof needs the structure
theory (minimal components are finite unions of intervals) plus the degenerate case `K ∩ J ≠ ∅`;
it is not written anywhere in the tree and, as it turns out, is not needed. And "no connection" is
not the property the transfer theorem needs: what it needs is "no periodic point of the left-limit
map `L`", which is strictly stronger than "no connection" (an `L`-cycle gives a connection).

**The argument that works (6 lines, elementary, new in §4.4).** Let `x₀ ∈ (a,b)` be `L`-periodic,
period `k ≥ 1`, `x_i := L^[i]x₀`. For `i < k` let `c_i` be the largest cut below `x_i` and
`ε := min_i (x_i − c_i) > 0`. Then `J_i := (x_i − ε, x_i) ⊆ (c_i, x_i]` contains no cut, so `T` is a
translation on `J_i`, by `δ_i`; and `x_i + δ_i = L(x_i) = x_{i+1}` by the explicit formula for `L`.
Hence `T '' J_i = J_{i+1}` **exactly** (indices mod `k`). So `T` permutes the `J_i` cyclically, each
`T|_{J_i}` being a translation: `λ|_K` for `K := ⋃_i J_i` is a `T`-invariant finite measure with
`λ(K) ≤ kε < 1`, and `T^[k]` is the identity on `J_0`. Hence `λ|_K/λ(K)` is a `T`-invariant
probability `≠ λ`, contradicting unique ergodicity. This is the classical "periodic orbits come in
families": a periodic left limit is a **periodic interval**. It gives `(H1) ⇒ (H2)` at every length
vector, needs no minimality, no Keane, no connections, no hyperplanes.

**What this removes from the plan.** `(H2)` is no longer a hypothesis of Theorem 2 (only `(H1)`
remains), `NoPeriodicLeftLimit` becomes a proved lemma (`noPeriodicLeftLimit_of_unique`), and the
module `AeNoPeriodic.lean` — Lemma 6.2 (proved in the previous round, .ultramath/smvz4odkr) plus the
null-hyperplane argument — is **not needed**: §6 is now an appendix recording it as an independent
a.e. proof. Milestones M5/M6 absorb the new lemma and M7 (`Main.lean`) no longer depends on it.

**Consistency check of the new lemma against the previous blueprint.** A periodic left limit is
still *necessary* to avoid (§8.3: it breaks uniform convergence, so a proof must exclude it); the
new lemma says unique ergodicity excludes it. The two together say: the case where the conclusion of
Theorem 2 fails is a case where `(H1)` already fails — which is exactly the situation one wants, and
it is why `(H2)` was never a real extra hypothesis.

### Addendum 127: `T̃` **is** uniquely ergodic on `[a+, b−]` — the author is right, my space was wrong

Instruction (verbatim): *"You write that T' is never uniquely ergodic, but I am not convinced. The
left end point a should *not* be split in two points, only the interior singularities should. Still,
if you want to split also the left end point in {0-, 0+}, then T' is a map on [0+, 1-], and this one
should be uniquely ergodic. Do you agree?"*

**Yes.** And the point is not cosmetic: my claim "`T̃` is never uniquely ergodic" was about the space
`X` of Blueprint 2 §2, which doubles *both* endpoints (because the split set is
`⋃_n T^n(s ∪ s' ∪ {b})` and `a ∈ s`). On `X` there are exactly two isolated points, `leftGerm a`
and `rightGerm b` (minimum and maximum of the order), and `T̃` fixes both (`L a = a`, `T b = b`), so
`δ` at either is an extra invariant measure. They are artefacts: they are the one-sided germs of the
endpoints, never approached from inside `[a,b)`. The correct object is

  `X° := closure (rightGerm '' Ico a b) = X ∖ {leftGerm a, rightGerm b}`  ("`[a+, b−]`"),

which is closed in `X`, hence compact, and `T̃`-invariant (`T̃` injective, and the two deleted points
have no other preimages). On it, `T̃` **is** uniquely ergodic when `T` is, with `rightGerm_*λ` as the
only invariant probability: this is the new **Theorem 4.11** of the blueprint, and its proof is three
lines from Theorem 4.6 + the lift lemma (Lemma 4.1) once the hypothesis `ν X° = 1` is stated
correctly.

**Bug this exposed, now fixed.** My earlier Theorem 4.6 was stated for `ν (closure (rightGerm '' [a,b])) = 1`,
and its proof claimed `rightGerm b ∉ K` — false, `rightGerm b` *is* in the closure of the right germs
of the closed interval (take `y = b`), so `δ_{rightGerm b}` was a counterexample to the statement as
written. With `K = X°` (half-open interval) both the statement and the `ρ {b} = 0` step are correct:
`ν {rightGerm b} = 0` because the point is deleted, and `ν {leftGerm b} = 0` by (H2) at `x = b`.

**Effect on the argument.** With Theorem 4.11 the source's own plan becomes literally valid: Tool 1
(Theorem 1.1) applied to the compact space `X°` and the continuous map `T̃|_{X°}`, whose unique
invariant measure is the lift of `λ`. Blueprint 2 §5 now records this as Route 1 and keeps the
relative form (Theorem 1.2) as Route 2; §8.2 is rewritten (the source's sentence is *true on the
right space*; what is not in the source is the space, the one-sided semi-conjugacy, and the ~20 lines
of transfer), Remark 2.7 and trap 14 warn against doubling the endpoints, and the Lean plan gains
`rightPart` / `uniqueErgodicOn_rightPart`.

### Addendum 128: dependency audit — Keane unused, and three gaps closed

Instruction (verbatim): *"What is the status with Keane? Is it still necessary? Is anything admitted
in the blueprint, or is it self-contained?"*

**Keane: not necessary, anywhere.** No proof in either blueprint mentions minimality, connections or
the structure theory of IETs. It survives only as a record in §8.6 (the true statement is Yoccoz
Theorem 5.9, "no connection ⇒ minimal", article p. 17; the converse is false for `d ≥ 3` by
Exercise 5.11 on the same page). The chain actually used is: `(H1)` ⟹ `(H2)` (Lemma 4.9, the
periodic-interval argument) ⟹ `T̃|_{X°}` uniquely ergodic (Theorem 4.11, from the defect identity and
the lift lemma) ⟹ uniform convergence (Tool 1) ⟹ `MasurVeechFun` a.e. (§7).

**Audit, and what it turned up.** New **§12** of Blueprint 2 lists, in one place, everything the two
blueprints use from outside themselves:

* the single mathematical input `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant_perm` (this repository, axiom-clean),
  i.e. hypothesis `(H1)`;
* the Mathlib facts: `instCompactSpaceProbabilityMeasure`, `tendsto_iff_forall_integral_tendsto`,
  `Measure.integral_map`, `Measure.ext_of_isPiSystem`,
  `ext_of_forall_integral_eq_of_IsFiniteMeasure` (via `HasOuterApproxClosed` for pseudo-metrizable
  spaces), the `SplitI` instance chain (`Pi.compactSpace`, `PseudoMetrizableSpace.subtype/pi`,
  `Subtype.borelSpace`, `Prod.borelSpace`, `Pi.borelSpace`), `birkhoffSum`/`birkhoffAverage`, and the
  `IsCutSet` API of `{CutSet,CutSetMeasure,IET}.lean` plus `Assembly.invariant_unitMeas`;
* and, for the appendix only, nullity of proper hyperplanes and Riesz representation.

Three gaps the audit exposed, all now closed:

1. **New Lemma 1.8** (elementary structure of `L`): `L x = x + δ_i` on `(c_i, c_{i+1}]`,
   `T x = x + δ_i` on `[c_i, c_{i+1})`; `L` maps `(c_i, c_{i+1}]` bijectively onto
   `(u_i, u_i + (c_{i+1} − c_i)]`, so `L` is a bijection of `[a,b]` fixing `a`; both maps are
   increasing translations on each open cell; `L` is left continuous, its discontinuities lie in `s`.
   This replaces three "prove separately" hints in §3.3–§3.4 (left continuity of `L`, injectivity of
   `L`, monotonicity on a cell).
2. **Positivity of the lengths is not needed.** Degenerate cells are allowed by `IsCutSet`
   (`isCutSet_mkIETCuts` asks for no positivity), and Lemmas 1.8, 4.9 and Theorem 2 never use it, so
   §7 no longer lists `∀ i, 0 < lam i` and trap 7 is rewritten. The a.e. input is only
   `lam ∈ simplexOn`, which is `ae_mem_simplexOn_of_card_ne_zero`.
3. **Lemma 3.4's surjectivity clause** is the one statement still written with a hint rather than a
   proof; it is **not used** (only injectivity is: Lemma 4.3 and Corollary 2.6), and §12.4 says so.

Conclusion of the audit: the blueprints are self-contained modulo Masur–Veech (the repository's own
theorem) and the listed Mathlib facts; no ergodic-theoretic or IET-theoretic theorem is admitted, in
particular not Keane's; and the only hypothesis of the upgraded theorem is `(H1)`.

### Addendum 135: `TransferConv`'s convergence hypothesis was unsatisfiable — repaired in place

Found by the orchestrator while preparing the discharge ledger, before any member reported it.

**Defect.** `uniqueErgodicFun_of_split` and `uniqueErgodicFun_of_proj` asked for uniform convergence
of the Birkhoff averages of `ψ` over **all** of `SplitI D` (`∀ z : SplitI D` / `S := Set.univ`). That
hypothesis is not dischargeable at the germ map, and no choice of `μ` repairs it:
`SplitI.rightPart D = X°` is `X ∖ {leftGerm 0, rightGerm 1}` (Blueprint 2, Lemma 2.4(vi)), both
deleted points are fixed by `T̃` (Corollary 2.6), and the concrete `germMapOf` really does fix them —
at `rightGerm 1` the new first coordinate is `T 1 = 1` and the side coordinate `decide (1 > d ∨ (1 = d
∧ side z = true))` is `true` exactly at `d = 1`, so the image is `rightGerm 1`; at `leftGerm 0` the
first coordinate is `L 0 = 0` and every coordinate is `false`, so the image is `leftGerm 0`. Uniform
convergence from a fixed point `z₀` forces `ψ z₀ = ∫ ψ dμ` for every continuous `ψ`, hence `μ = δ_{z₀}`,
which contradicts `μ.map proj = unitMeas`. Tool 1 can only supply convergence **on `rightPart`** (it is
applied to the subtype `↥(rightPart D)`, which is compact by `SplitI.isCompact_rightPart`).

So the landed theorem was true but useless: an implication whose hypothesis the endgame cannot prove.
This is precisely the failure mode that a "stronger than the source" hypothesis produces, and it would
have surfaced only at the assembly, one round later.

**Repair, landed.** The convergence hypothesis is now asked on a set: `uniqueErgodicFun_of_split` gained
`(S : Set X) (hS : ∀ x ∈ Ico 0 1, sec x ∈ S)` and `hconv : ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ z ∈ S, …`; it passes `S` to
`tendsto_uniform_birkhoffAverage_of_section`, whose `h` was already `S`-restricted. `uniqueErgodicFun_of_proj`
instantiates `S := SplitI.rightPart D`, discharging `hS` by `SplitI.rightGerm_mem_rightPart` (after
`clipI_of_mem`), and its own `hconv` now reads `∀ z ∈ SplitI.rightPart D`. This is a *weaker hypothesis*,
i.e. a strictly stronger theorem, in the direction the campaign needs; no conclusion changed and no
hypothesis was added to hide work. `lake build`: 8782 jobs, 0 warnings, all eight `#print axioms`
reports clean.

The doc of `uniqueErgodicFun_of_split` now states in prose why the restriction is there (Remark 2.7),
so that a later reader does not "simplify" it back to `Set.univ`. Note this also means `IET.lean` must
supply `hconv` in the subtype form — `tendsto_uniform_birkhoffAverage` at `X := ↥(rightPart D)` with
`μ' := μ.comap Subtype.val` — which is what the audit `smvz7lj5k` had already verified is instantiable
with exactly the two `haveI`s (`Countable D`, `CompactSpace ↥(rightPart D)`).

### Addendum 140: `masurVeechFun` is proved — the Birkhoff-averages form of Masur–Veech is formalised

**`UniformConvergence/IET.lean` landed. `masurVeechFun : MasurVeechFun`, with
`#print axioms` reporting exactly `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.** `lake build`: 8786 jobs,
0 warnings. The deferred item D1 of `blueprint.md` — the Birkhoff bridge from "unique invariant
probability measure" to "uniform Birkhoff averages of every continuous test function" — is closed, and
`IET2/ChallengeWeak.lean`'s `MasurVeechFun` is now a theorem of the `MasurVeech` project.

The final term is three lines:

```lean
theorem masurVeechFun : MasurVeechFun :=
  masurVeechFun_of_pointwise fun lam π hsum hH1 =>
    uniqueErgodicFun_of_unique_invariant lam π hsum hH1
```

with `masurVeechFun_of_pointwise` (Addendum 133, from `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant_perm` by a.e.
transfer) and `uniqueErgodicFun_of_unique_invariant` = Theorem 2. What the file contains:

* **`map_proj_eq_unitMeas_of_invariant`** — the measure-theoretic core of Theorem 4.11. It pushes a
  `T̃`-invariant probability on `↥(rightPart D)` to the split space, applies
  `Transfer.map_map_eq_self` with the jump set `J = {x ∈ Icc 0 1 | leftLimit x ≠ T x}`
  (`Finset.filter` of `s ∪ {1}`), and kills the jump mass: at `c ≠ 0` by
  `measure_singleton_eq_zero_of_injOn_orbit` fed by `germMap_orbit_infinite`, at `c = 0` because
  `leftGerm 0 ∉ rightPart` while the measure lives on the subtype. Then (H1) gives
  `ν.map proj = Assembly.unitMeas`.
* **`uniqueErgodicOn_rightPart`** — **Theorem 4.11**: the only invariant probability on `[0⁺, 1⁻]` is
  the lift of Lebesgue measure, by `MeasPrep.lift_unique_on_Ico` (`unitMeas_singleton` and
  `unitMeas_Ico` as its two side conditions, `SplitI.eq_of_proj_eq_of_notMem` as its injectivity).
* **`uniqueErgodicFun_of_unique_invariant`** — **Theorem 2**: Tool 1 at `X := ↥(rightPart D)` for the
  restricted germ map, whose unique invariant measure is `μ₀`; `TransferConv.uniqueErgodicFun_of_proj`
  (with its convergence hypothesis restricted to `rightPart`, the repair of Addendum 135) converts the
  uniform convergence on the split interval into `UniqueErgodicFun (mkIETFun lam π 0)`, and
  `SubtypeConv.forall_mem_rightPart_of_subtype` bridges the subtype wording to the `S`-restricted one.

### Addendum 145: the (H2) audit answers the one question — the scope is exactly right — and two SPEC statements are false

`smvz92yjt` (audit of `Limits.lean`) exhausted its calls with `.ultramath/smvz92yjt/m1/AUDIT-LIMITS.md`
(24 KB), a baseline copy that recompiles the file warning-free, counterexample files, and a scope probe.

**The question I asked it: is `NoPeriodicLeftLimit` the (H2) the campaign needs, at the scope it needs?
Answer: yes, exactly.** It proved the point in three steps rather than asserting it:
`NoPeriodicLeftLimit` is *definitionally* the blueprint's (H2) (`Fidelity.lean` closes the SPEC text by
`rfl`, same binder order, same `Ioc a b`, same `0 < k`); the exclusion of `0` is not a weakening but a
necessity, since `(leftLimit h)^[k] a = a` for **every** cut set and every `k`
(`leftLimit_of_le h le_rfl`), so the `Icc` version of (H2) is *false* and Corollary 4.10 would have been
unprovable had (H2) been stated on `Icc`; and every point of the endgame's jump set is covered —
`Icc 0 1 = {0} ∪ Ioc 0 1` is a set identity it proved, `(0,1]` is (H2)'s business, and `0` is disposed
of by `leftGerm 0 ∉ rightPart`, with no dynamical hypothesis at `0` at all. It also checked the two
branches are *both live*: it exhibits a cut set with `L 0 = 0 ≠ 1/2 = T 0` (so `0` really can be a
jump) and observes that `1 ∈ Ioc 0 1` so (H2) covers `1`, which is where `IET.lean` uses it. Conclusion:
"no point of any interval is missing".

**Two statements in `SPEC.md` §2 P2 were false, and it proved that with counterexamples.** The landed
declarations deviate from the SPEC, and the deviations are forced corrections:
* `leftLimit_eq_apply` with `x ∈ Icc a b` is **false at `x = b`** (`L b` is the top of the last cell's
  image, `f b` is junk, and `b ∉ s` always); `Counterexample.lean:SPEC_leftLimit_eq_apply_Icc_false`
  compiles the refutation. The landed form is on `Ico a b`, which is what every consumer needs.
* `leftLimit_injOn` **without** `Function.Injective f` is **false** (blueprint Remark 1.9's
  non-injective exchange has `L (3/4) = L (5/4)`); `SPEC_leftLimit_injOn_false` compiles it. The landed
  form carries the injectivity hypothesis, reported in its docstring, and the campaign discharges it
  with `T.injective` (`mkIETEquiv` is an `Equiv`) at the two places where it is load-bearing.
I have corrected `SPEC.md` at both points, with a comment naming the audit and the counterexample, so a
later reader cannot re-introduce the false forms.

**Two docstring defects, both fixed.** F1 was mine: the `jumpSet` I added in Addendum 137 hard-codes
the right endpoint to `1`, so it is Definition 1.4 for `b = 1` and *not* for general `b` (the audit
proved that for `b = 2` the point `b` is a jump it misses), and its docstring additionally claimed to be
"the form in which the transfer theorem consumes the jump set", which is false — `IET.lean` builds its
own from `finite_jumpSet`. The docstring now says all of that, including that nothing consumes it. F2:
`leftLimit`'s docstring claimed the one-sided-limit description for all `x > a`, false for `x > b`
(where the cell formula runs past the last cell); it now says the limit description is on `Ioc a b` and
that no proof evaluates `leftLimit` outside `Icc a b`.

### Addendum 146: the split interval now *proves* its own convention

`smvz94nqt` (audit of `Split.lean`) exhausted its calls *before* writing its report — it left seven
compiling probes and a `deletions/` directory and nothing else. That looked like a wasted slot until
I read the probes: `ProbeCAll.lean` compiles (0 errors) and contains, proved, exactly the facts that
were missing from the library.

**Landed in `Split.lean`, in a new `SplitI` section "The one-sided behaviour of the germs"** (proofs
taken unchanged from the probe, only the namespace adapted, and `#print axioms` added for each):

* `SplitI.tendsto_rightGerm_nhdsLT`: `rightGerm y → leftGerm x` as `y ↑ x` — **Blueprint 2 Lemma
  2.4(v), left half**, which the probe's header records as "absent from the whole repository";
* `SplitI.tendsto_rightGerm_nhdsGT`: `rightGerm y → rightGerm x` as `y ↓ x` — the right half;
* `SplitI.rightGerm_ne_leftGerm`: the two germs differ at a split point (Lemma 2.4(iv), the doubling);
* `SplitI.side_eq_coord` and `SplitI.side_eq_true`: `side` is the blueprint's `χ ⟨x, _⟩` on `D` and
  `true` off it — **the formula itself**, not a docstring claim;
* `SplitI.upSet_eq_blueprint`, `SplitI.downSet_eq_blueprint`: `U⁺`/`U⁻` are the displayed sets of
  Blueprint §2.3;
* plus their coordinate-level helpers (`eventually_coord_nhdsLT/_GT`, `tendsto_rightGerm_coe_*`).

Why this mattered enough to land: every audit of the campaign flagged the same residual risk — the
left/right convention of `side`, and therefore of the germ map's second coordinate, is the one thing
that **every proof in the campaign would still satisfy if it had been mirrored**, because a global
reversal is internally consistent. I had checked it by hand against the blueprint's printed formulas,
and the `Germ` audit had confirmed the germ map equals Definition 3.1 (which is sensitive to `side`).
With these six lemmas the convention is now *derived*: the point named `rightGerm x` is the one
approached by the right germs of `y > x`, `leftGerm x` the one approached by the right germs of
`y < x`, and `side` is literally `χ`'s value. A mirrored convention is now refutable inside the
library rather than by reading.

The probe also contains refutations (that `x ∈ D` is not idle in `isOpen_upSet`/`isOpen_downSet`, that
both hypotheses of `ext` are needed, that `rightGerm_eq_leftGerm` fails on `D`, that
`rightGerm 1 ∈ rightPart` exactly when `1 ∈ D`). They are audit evidence and stay in the probe rather
than in the library.

### Addendum 148: the Transfer audit closes the last question — the defect identity has the blueprint's sign

`smvz94i1k` (audit of `Transfer.lean`) submitted and was accepted. It is the audit I most wanted,
because it checks the one thing the campaign's own proofs could *never* catch: the sign of the defect
identity. A sign error there is invisible downstream, since the sum vanishes in the only consumer.

**Verdict: no blocking defect; fidelity passes.** What it established, with compiled evidence:

* **The sign is right.** It built a concrete non-vacuous instance of the landed identity where both
  sides are `1/2`, and where the opposite sign would give `-1/2` (`probes/P3_model.lean`). I re-ran
  that file myself. It also confirms the argument order (mass times difference, `g (L c) - g (T c)`)
  and that `defect_identity` and `map_map_eq_self` share one index set `J` with `hdef`/`hTeq`/`hvan`.
* **`map_map_eq_self` is right-sized for its consumer**: the conclusion is the full measure equality,
  `hvan` is the only place the jump mass enters, `J` is the caller's `Finset` (so `J = ∅` needs no mass
  hypothesis), the proof tests bounded **Borel** functions (`A.indicator 1`) rather than continuous
  ones, and only `Measurable T` is assumed. All fourteen hypotheses are discharged at `IET.lean`.
* **`lift_unique` is the blueprint's Lemma 4.1 and is true and non-vacuous** (`lift_unique_nonvacuous`
  compiles); its single defect is the *total*-section hypothesis, and `no_total_section` compiles the
  proof that no total section of `SplitI.proj` exists. That is the cleanest justification on record for
  having written `MeasPrep.lift_unique_on_Ico`.
* **It validated its own instrument**: `P0_controls.lean` shows a deliberately `sorry`-ed theorem *is*
  reported as `sorryAx` under this repository's `warn.sorry = false`. Two earlier audits reported the
  trap; this one measured it.

Findings and what I did:

* **F2, fixed.** `defect_identity`'s docstring said it was stated "as in the specification", but the
  landed form adds `hT : Measurable T` and `hpe : ∀ c ∈ J, p (e c) = c` — both discharged at
  `IET.lean`, both necessary for the proof (`hpe` is what makes `e` injective on `J`, so the sum does
  not count an atom twice). SPEC §3 asks for such additions to be *reported*; the docstring now says
  exactly which two were added, why, and that `hGinj` is carried but unused by this statement.
* **F1, recorded not acted on.** `hGinj` is idle in `map_map_eq_self`, `defect_identity` and
  `defect_identity_meas`; the auditor compiled the removal from all three and both call sites. On the
  critical path this makes `IET.lean` supply the whole of Lemma 3.4 for nothing. Removing it would be a
  strict improvement, but it changes the binder list of landed, already-audited declarations to delete
  a hypothesis every consumer already supplies — library hygiene, not correctness — so the final tree
  is not being destabilised for it.
* **F5, worth knowing**: the topology kept in the section variable is used only to synthesise
  `MeasurableSingletonClass X`, and `[CompactSpace X]` is inert in all seven declarations of the file.
  The module docstring's "compact Hausdorff space" framing overstates the interface.
* **F7/F8**: `lift_unique` and `map_section_invariant` remain unused by the campaign, and landed
  `map_map_eq_self` concludes the invariance half of Blueprint Theorem 4.6 (the identification with
  `λ` is supplied by `IET.lean` from (H1)) — honest content, generous labelling.

# The `IsSmallRelation` bound: `4` cannot be lowered to `2`, but it can be lowered to `3`

The question, asked directly: does replacing `4` by `2` in `IsSmallRelation` break the development,
or can all the proofs be repaired?  Run in copies under `IET2/.scratch/exp/` (nothing below was landed
in `IET2/`; the tree above is untouched).  Full write-up: `IET2/.scratch/exp/README.md`.

**`2` is impossible, and not for want of proof technique: the statement of Case 1b of Lemma 3.2 is
false at bound `2`.**  At bound `2`, `¬ IsBadParam` only excludes relations among the *free*
coordinates with coefficients `≤ 2`, while Case 1b produces a relation among *all* the lengths whose
coefficients are `≤ 2` (`[π i < π k] + [π i < π m] - [i < m]`) but whose free-coordinate coefficients
reach `3`.  Counterexample, formalised and axiom-clean in
`.scratch/exp/small2/IETFree/BoundTwoRefute.lean`
(`IETFree.not_splitting_of_imageLeft_relation_add_two`): `d = e = 2`, both permutations `(0 1)`,
`k = m = l = 0`, `n = 1`, `lam = (5/8, 3/8)`, `mu = (7/8, 1/8)`.  The relation of Case 1b reads
`3/8 + 1/8 + 3/8 = 7/8`, the pair is good at bound `2` (a relation `c + a λ₀ + b μ₀ = 0` with
`|c|, |a|, |b| ≤ 2` forces `8c + 5a + 7b = 0`, hence `c = a = b = 0`), and the conclusion fails
(`σ 0 = 1` is not `< n = 1`).  The pair is bad at bound `3`, through `3 - 2λ₀ - 2μ₀ = 0`, so this is
exactly where the threshold sits.  The same data also satisfy the hypotheses of
`IETDatum.pairSplitting_of_mark_preimage` with `c = 1/2` (checked by hand), so Case 1b's geometric
form fails at bound `2` as well.

The general bridge lemma is false at bound `2` too, independently of Case 1b: `relation_of_good` in
its old form (full-coefficient bound `2`) fails at `lam = (1/4, 3/4)`, `mu = (√2 - 1, 2 - √2)`,
`a = (2, -2)`, `b = (1, 1)` (hand-verified, not formalised).  At bound `3` it is still false
(that example needs free coefficients `4`), which is why the bound-`3` version *states the bound on the
free coefficients* instead of deriving it.

**`3` works.**  `.scratch/exp/small3/` carries the change and `./Build.sh` there is green: 32 modules
`ok`, no warnings, comparator `OK` (32 661 declarations), `sorryAx: 6` (3 `Challenge` + 3
`ChallengeWeak`, library `0`), `main` on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.  The change is
three files (`logs/bound3.patch`, ~340 diff lines):
* the bound `4` → `3` in the three fields of `IsSmallRelation`, in `smallCoeffs`, `mem_smallCoeffs`
  and in the hypotheses of `coeffs_zero_of_good_with_const`;
* `relation_of_good` restated at full-coefficient bound `1` and a new
  `relation_of_good_of_free_coeffs` (free coefficients and constant `≤ 3`) proved directly from
  `coeffs_zero_of_good_with_const`; Case 1a, Case 2a and `Presentation.leftEnd_ne_sum_lam_of_good`
  use the first, Case 1b the second;
* Case 1b's three free-coefficient bounds proved from the indicator shapes (new helpers
  `abs_add_sub_le_three`, `abs_sub_sub_le_three` in `BlockIrreducibility`).
`isBadParam_mem_badSet`'s `hN : 4 ≤ N` and `ae_goodParams_real`'s `max N₀ 4` need no change (any
`N ≥ 3` works), so the tube width stays `4`.

What survives at bound `2` besides Case 1b, for the record: `ReductionData`'s three fields,
`smallCoeffs`, `mem_smallCoeffs`, `coeffs_zero_of_good_with_const`, `relation_of_good` (restated at
`≤ 1`), `Presentation`'s two `have`s and Case 2a's two `have`s.  Every module up to and including
`BlockData` is then green, `BlockIrreducibility` fails at exactly one obligation (line 375, Case 1b),
and the four modules after it (`BlockAssembly`, `BlockDatum`, `BlockLemma`, `ChallengeWeakSolved`)
cannot be checked at bound `2` at all, since they import it.  Nothing here restates the paper's Lemma
3.2 differently: `splitting_of_imageLeft_relation_add`'s statement is byte-identical at bound `3`, and
only its proof changes.

from the pre-merge project — it set only `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet`.  On the merged tree
`runLinter IETFree` reported **11 findings in 2 614 declarations** (plus 2 055 automatically generated
ones, 14 linters); `runLinter Challenge` passed at once.

What was found and done:

* `docBlame` (2): docstrings added to the two data fields `IETDatum₂.piTop` / `piBottom`.
* `simpNF` (1): **`birkhoffMeasure_apply_univ` is deleted** — `simp` proves its statement from
  `MeasureTheory.measure_univ`, it was `@[simp]` and unused; nothing else referenced it.
* `unusedArguments` (8 declarations, 11 arguments), all removed from the statements:
  `Assembly.lambdaOf_lebesgue` (`[NeZero n]`), `piEquivMeas` (`[Fintype α]`),
  `Stopping.Mk_card_eq_mmin` and `Stopping.exists_stopfam_of_good` (`[Nonempty α]`),
  the private `IETDatum₂.Path.Emat` (`[Fintype α]`), `lift_unique_on_Ico`
  (`[BorelSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [T2Space X] [IsProbabilityMeasure lam]`),
  `measure_singleton_map` (`[IsProbabilityMeasure ν]`), `lift_unique`
  (`[IsProbabilityMeasure lam] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]`).  Every one was unused in the *value* as

**The cascade is real, and it moves in both directions.** 11 → 2 → 0: removing `[Nonempty α]` from

characters.  **Check `lake build` after every round, not just `runLinter`** — both warnings were

### Addendum 152: dead-code pruning along the declaration graph

**Method.** `IETFree/ChallengeSolved.lean` imports the whole library, so module-level liveness is the
import closure of that one file; declaration-level liveness is the transitive closure of
`Expr.getUsedConstants` over type *and* value (proofs included, constructors of inductives added, as
`Comparator.runForUsedConsts` does) from the roots `main`, `coe_mkIETEquiv`, `mkIETEquiv`.  A
`#eval`-driven probe (`import IETFree`, `getEnv`, `env.getModuleIdxFor?` to keep only project
constants) produced the dead list; a text scanner with `namespace`/`end` tracking turned names into
line ranges, and the blocks were deleted with their docstrings, `@[simp]` attributes and
`omit … in` preambles (adjacent ranges merged; a first attempt swallowed neighbouring declarations
because a declaration line starting with `@[` looked like a preamble — the diff against
`.scratch/integ/backup/IETFree.preprune` caught it).

**What went.** One module (`MainCounterexample`: not imported by anything in the closure — the
counterexample that motivated `μ (Ico 0 1) = 1` is not in the library, and the three docstrings
that cited it now state what it asserted) and **80 declarations** (609 lines), including a dead chunk of
`UniformConvergence/Limits` (`jumpSet` and its API), `IETDatum₂.name`/`secondary`, `TowerN.floor`/
`countUp`/`permAfter`/`lamAfter`, `NestedCylinder.CylTree` with its `W`, the `Tower.piN`/`lamN` family,
`Transfer.lift_unique`/`map_section_invariant`/`defect_identity`, and `birkhoffMeasure_apply_univ`.
Eleven `/-! ## … -/` headers were left empty by the deletions and were removed.

**What the graph cannot see, and what was kept (17).** A `@[simp]` lemma whose proof is `rfl` is
applied by `simp` *definitionally*, so it leaves no trace in the proof term: the graph calls it dead
while a live proof needs it. The build is the oracle — each of these was put back after `lake build`
rejected its removal:

`IETDatum₂.{vertex_nil, vertex_singleton, ofPerm_piTop, ofPerm_piBottom, inv_piTop, inv_piBottom,
inv_inv, inv_last_true}`, `Tower.{lamAfter_nil, toComb_last_false, toComb_last_true}`,

### Addendum 153: the challenge loses `imageLengths` and `leftEnd_zero`; `idx` inlined

Owner's rulings (this session): remove `imageLengths` from `Challenge.lean` (unreachable from the
targets, hence never compared); remove `leftEnd_zero` there and inline its use in `idx`'s proof,
"which will probably need to be duplicated in the library definition of `idx`"; and reword the
docstrings of `mkIETFun`/`mkIETEquiv` to open with **The interval exchange transformation**, as a
bare function / as an equiv.

Why the duplication is needed: `idx` is *reachable* (from `coe_mkIETEquiv`'s statement through
`mkIETFun`), so the comparator compares its whole `ConstantInfo` including the value — the proof
term.  The library's `idx` therefore had to stop mentioning `leftEnd_zero` too, even though the
library keeps that lemma (12 other uses, in `Pair/` and in `IET.lean` itself).  Both proofs are
now

```lean
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  simp only [idxSet, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  simpa [leftEnd] using hx
```

`Challenge.lean` no longer declares `imageLengths` or `leftEnd_zero`; the library still declares both,
and neither is reachable from the targets, so nothing is compared.  The comparator's count drops by
one (30 900 → **30 899** declarations) — the `leftEnd_zero` that used to be reached through `idx`'s
value.  Docstrings do not enter `ConstantInfo`, but the challenge's copies keep the library's text.

`OK` on 30 899 declarations; `runLinter Challenge` and `runLinter IETFree` pass.

### Addendum 154: `Build.sh` is now `SlowBuild.sh`, and it is not the build

**Owner's ruling (this session):** "Don't delete it, but rename it to something like SlowBuild.sh. I am
still happy to have it for thorough checks and comparator, but you will never run it unless I tell you
explicitly to do it. Explain its new status in README/NOTES."

**Status.** `./SlowBuild.sh` is the *thorough check*, not the build. `lake build` is the build —
incremental (hash-based), parallel over the four cores, seconds for an ordinary edit and under three
minutes from a removed `.lake/build`. `SlowBuild.sh` is deliberately the opposite: plain `lean`, one
process per module, in dependency order, everything recompiled every run, Mathlib reloaded per module,
several minutes in total. It is worth its cost in exactly three situations, which is why it is kept:
a `sorry` count (it compiles with `warn.sorry` on, whereas the lakefile silences those warnings),
`--strict` (fails if `sorryAx` is reachable from `main`), and `Comparator/Check.lean` on the two
compiled modules. **It is run only on the owner's explicit request.**

**Why `lake build` works here — the reason `Build.sh` was ever written, now understood.** This VM's
`.lake/packages/mathlib/.lake/build/lib/lean` already contains Mathlib's oleans (root-owned, from the
image), so Lake sees the pinned git package as fully built and needs no local write. The old header's
premise — "Lake cannot use `/opt/mathlib` as a package, so compile with plain `lean`" — was true only
in the sense that Lake may not *rewrite* those directories: a change of Mathlib revision would still
need `lake exe cache get` (or a `path = "/opt/mathlib"` require) before `lake build` can succeed.

**What the ordinary loop is now.** `lake build` (whole tree or `lake build IETFree.<module>` for a
targeted check); `LEAN_PATH="$PWD/.lake/build/lib/lean:$PWD:$LEAN_PATH" lake env
lean --run Comparator/Check.lean` (~40 s) after a change to `Challenge.lean`, to a statement, or to a
declaration reachable from `main`; `rg -n '\bsorry\b' IETFree` (0 hits) for the "no sorry in the
library" claim, with the `#print axioms main` line that `lake build` itself prints covering
reachability; `runLinter` when declarations change; one `rm -rf .lake/build && lake build` before any
claim of zero warnings, because warnings are only emitted for modules that are actually recompiled.

**Renamed, not rewritten.** The script's body is unchanged apart from its header comment and the two
usage lines in it; `bash -n` passes (there is no `--help` flag: any argument other than `--strict` is
ignored, so invoking it always runs the full build). One operational note stays: its module list is a
snapshot of `IETFree.lean`'s imports taken at start-up, so it must not run concurrently with a rename or
a move (that is how one of its runs failed during the `PrefixWord` rename). `README.md`,
`Comparator/README.md`, `Comparator/Check.lean`'s docstring and `formalization.yaml` were updated to the
new name and status.

### Addendum 159: a total `mkIET1`, statements without the simplex hypothesis, and one `open` line per file

Owner's instructions: *"`mkIET1 lam π` … is ugly because of the assumption `h`, which is automatically
satisfied ae but is necessary to write down `mkIET1 lam π h`.  You will rename the current `mkIET1` to
`mkIET1'`, and define a new total function `mkIET1 lam π`, defined as `mkIET1' lam π h` if `lam`
belongs to the simplex, and the identity `IET` otherwise.  Use it throughout to clean up the
statements and the proofs, relying on the lemma that says that for ae `lam` for `simplexVolume d`,
then `lam` belongs to `simplex d`."*

**Renamed and added** (`IET.lean`): the old `mkIET1` is now `mkIET1'`, and its API lemmas are primed
with it (`coe_mkIET1'`).  The new `mkIET1 lam π` is `if h : ∑ i, lam i = 1 then mkIET1' lam π h else 1`,
with `mkIET1_of_mem`, `mkIET1_of_notMem` and `coe_mkIET1` (its function on the simplex is
`mkIETFun lam π 0`).  All 355 uses in the library were renamed to `mkIET1'` in one pass, so nothing
else changed meaning.

**Statements cleaned** (the `∀ h : lam ∈ simplex` disappears, the a.e. membership does the work):

* `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant_perm` — `∀ᵐ lam, ∃! μ, Invariant μ (mkIET1 lam π) ∧ …`, from
  `ae_mem_simplexOn_fin` and `mkIET1_of_mem`;
* `uniqueErgodic_of_unique_invariant` (Theorem 2) — concludes `UniqueErgodic (mkIET1 lam π)`;
* `masurVeech` — `∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolume d), UniqueErgodic (mkIET1 lam π)`;
* `veechRigidity` — `∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolume d), IsRigidByTranslations (mkIET1 lam π)`;
* `BlockGood` — `UniqueErgodic (mkIET1 lam τ) ∧ IsRigidByTranslations (mkIET1 lam τ)`.

One place kept the old shape deliberately: the two hypotheses `hue`/`hrig` of
`GoodRegion.exists_word_trivial_of_region`.  Written with the total `mkIET1 (B.lam hq) B.perm`, that
statement no longer elaborates within the default heartbeat limit (the `dite` in `mkIET1` forces whnf
on the block's dependent length vector), and raising `maxHeartbeats` is against the campaign's rules;
the conversion is done instead at the single call site, by `simpa only [mkIET1_of_mem h]`.

**`richGreedyPath`** also lost its right-of-the-colon binders: it is now
`(P) (hP) (hn) (π₀ : IETDatum₂ α n) (u : List Bool) (hu : vertex P u = π₀) (γ₀ : List Bool) :
∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolumeOn α), ∀ k, …`, with the witness `u` replacing the existential.  A scan of
every theorem statement in the library (conclusions beginning with `∀`/a binder) found no other
variable binder right of the colon: what remains are index quantifiers (`∀ i`, `∀ k`, `∀ ε > 0`,
`∀ᵐ`, `∀ᶠ`) and hypotheses, which cannot move.

**`open` lines.**  Every file now has a single `open` line and a single `open scoped` line, adjacent,
before the first declaration (21 files were rewritten, e.g. `LevelN.lean`:
`open MeasureTheory Finset` / `open scoped BigOperators ENNReal NNReal`).  Mid-file `open`s that
introduced names not in the file prefix (`open Tower`, `open IETDatum₂`, `open Classical in`, …) were
left where they are.

**Checks.**  `lake build` green, 8823 jobs; `main` still `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`;
`Comparator/Check.lean` accepts the pair; the ten touched modules compile warning-free; every line of
the library is ≤ 100 characters (the rename made eight lines one character too long; all re-wrapped).
Declarations 4 522 → 4 530 (the total `mkIET1` and its three lemmas), reachable 3 987 → 3 992,
lines 46 282 → 46 275.

**Follow-up: the same for `have`.**  *"Inside proofs, you can also move binders left of the colon.
`have h (i : ℕ) : ...` is perfectly fine syntax, and should be used whenever possible."*  Done by a
scripted pass over the 21 files that had it: every `have h : ∀ (x : X) (y : Y), B` became
`have h (x : X) (y : Y) : B` (58 sites), with the matching `intro`/`fun` prefix removed from the
proof (34 by script, the rest by hand where the intros were partial, implicit binders were involved

list and moving it buys nothing, and `SubintervalTransfer.key`, whose binder list would exceed the
line limit.  `lake build` green at 8823 jobs, all files warning-free, lines 46 275 → 46 256.

**And the arrow antecedents of a `have`.**  *"you should change it to `have hmax (q : FreeGroup
α) (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (hq : v = q ^ k) : k ≤ k₀ := by`"*.  Applied where the pattern is
unambiguous — a `have` whose type is a chain of arrows, with no leading `∀` and no binder list
inside an antecedent, and whose proof opens with `intro` naming exactly those hypotheses:
`Centralizer.hmax`/`hmax'`, `MeasureTools.key`, `SubintervalTransfer.hblk`,
`BlockIrreducibility.hm0_case`, `RauzyReach.hf` (6 sites; the intros disappear).  A first bulk pass
with a looser parser was **reverted** — it mis-read `∀ ⦃n m : ℕ⦄` binders as hypotheses and
broke 49 places; the tree was restored from `IET2.zip` and the pass redone under the stricter rule.
The remaining ~390 `have`s of this shape (types beginning with `∀`, patterns in the intro, or an
antecedent containing a binder list) need per-site judgement and are **not** done; lines 46 256 →
46 250.

**The rest of them (owner's instruction).**  *"do the remaining ~390 have-binder conversions file by
file with a build after each.  Be careful to start with the files that are latest in the import
order, and do only recompile the file which you've just tweaked."*  Done exactly in that order —
reverse topological order of `IETFree.lean`'s imports, one file at a time, each compiled alone with
`lake env lean … -o` (never a library build until the end), so every edit cost one file.  A script
parsed each `have`'s type — a leading `∀` chain with `( )`, `{ }`, `⦃ ⦄` or bare `x : T` binders,
then a chain of `→` antecedents — moved both into the binder list (binder kinds preserved, antecedents
named from the proof's `intro`), and dropped the consumed intros.  **46 files, 129 conversions**, over
three iterations of the script (bare binders and `⦃ ⦄` binders were mishandled at first; each bad pass
was reverted file by file from its backup).  `GoodRegion.lean` needed one site by hand
(`hGgf`, whose binders resume after an arrow).  Eight lines went over 100 characters and were
re-wrapped.  Checks: `lake build` green at 8823 jobs, the 46 files warning-free under the lakefile's
options, `main` still `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, declarations and reachability
unchanged (4 530 / 3 992), lines 46 250 → 46 138.

**`StraddleMass` and `StraddleMassCard` are deleted too.**  Owner's instruction, after the check in
the previous entry: *"Now do the same for StraddleMassCard and StraddleMass: remove them and discharge
at the use sites."*  (The check mattered: `StraddleMassCard` is *not* an induction hypothesis — no
lemma proves `StraddleMassCard P (k+1)` from it at `k`; the induction in this part of the library runs
on `Graded P k C`, whose step is `InductionStep`, and `graded_exists` is its generic "base + step ⟹
all `k`" form.  `StraddleMassCard` is proved independently, and uniformly, for every `k`.)

**Deleted** (`RichPath/StraddleMass.lean`): `def StraddleMass`, `def StraddleMassCard`,
`straddleMass_iff`, `straddleMassCard_zero`, `straddleMassCard_one`,

### Addendum 161: `UniqueErgodic` is the weak form; Lemma 2.9 moves to `UniformConvergence`

Owner's instruction (4 November): *"In the file Pair/Irreducible, the definition of UniqueErgodic
is the strong form of uniform convergence of Birkhoff averages of continuous functions.  I'd rather
have the definition of UniqueErgodic to be the weak form there, existence of a unique invariant
probability measure.  It should be moved to the file IET.lean, so that it can be shared between the
directories UniformConvergence and Pair.  The use site in Pair is to prove exists_uniform_birkhoff.
I'd rather have this lemma in the UniformConvergence directory as it is not a statement about
pairs."*

(The definition was in `IETFree/Basic.lean`, not in `Pair/Irreducible.lean`: Addendum 158 moved it
there to break the import cycle.  The instruction applies verbatim, and `IET.lean` is below both
consumers.)

**The two forms, separated.**  `UniqueErgodic f` (`IETFree/IET.lean`, with `Invariant`) is now
Definition 2.1 as the paper states it: `∃! μ : ProbabilityMeasure ℝ, Invariant μ f ∧ μ (Ico 0 1) =
1`.  The mass condition is not decoration — an exchange is the identity off `[0, 1)`, so without it
every exchange has the Dirac mass at `2` invariant alongside Lebesgue's.  The strong form is a
**separate predicate**, `UniformBirkhoff f` (`UniformConvergence/Basic.lean`): the Birkhoff
averages of every continuous `ψ` converge to `∫ ψ d unitMeas` uniformly on `[0, 1)`, stated with
the iterate `f^[n]` that the transfer argument uses.  `uniqueErgodic_iff_birkhoffAverage`, whose
only content was the rewriting between the group power and the iterate, is gone.

`UniformBirkhoff` is a definition, not a hypothesis in disguise: it is *proved* from
`UniqueErgodic` (`uniformBirkhoff_of_uniqueErgodic`) and it is assumed by no theorem of the tree —
the rule of Addendum 156 forbids assuming a statement that has been proved unconditionally, and
nothing has.

**Theorems, renamed with their conclusions.**  `uniqueErgodic_of_split` / `uniqueErgodic_of_proj`
are `uniformBirkhoff_of_split` / `uniformBirkhoff_of_proj` and conclude `UniformBirkhoff T`; they
now also lose their `rw [uniqueErgodic_iff_birkhoffAverage]`.  Theorem 2
`uniqueErgodic_of_unique_invariant` is `uniformBirkhoff_mkIET1`, with the hypothesis `UniqueErgodic
(mkIET1 lam π)`; its first step, new there, *derives* the identification of the unique invariant
probability with Lebesgue measure (`Assembly.invariant_unitMeas`, `unitMeas_Ico`, and the
uniqueness) — that block used to be the body of `masurVeech` in `Pair/Irreducible.lean`.  The new
`uniformBirkhoff_of_uniqueErgodic (f : IET 0 1)` extends Theorem 2 to an arbitrary exchange by
re-presenting it as `mkIETEquiv lam π 0` (`exists_mkIETEquiv_eq`) and transporting along the
equality of the underlying functions; it is the only new proof of the round.

**Lemma 2.9 moves.**  `exists_uniform_birkhoff` is `UniformConvergence/IET.lean`'s now, statement
unchanged (a finite union of half-open intervals `S`, `unitMeas.real S ≤ ε`, an `N` with a uniform
bound `2ε` on the Birkhoff sums of the indicator), hypothesis `UniqueErgodic f` — the weak form —
and proof unchanged apart from `uniformBirkhoff_of_uniqueErgodic` supplying the convergence.  Its
notion `IsFiniteUnionIntervals` moved from `Pair/MeasureTools.lean` to `IETFree/CutSet.lean`, for
the same reason: it is a statement about subsets of `ℝ`, `UniformConvergence/` may not import
`Pair/`, and `Pair/MeasureTools.lean` keeps the API lemma that produces it
(`isFiniteUnionIntervals_ne_id`).

**What `Pair/` keeps.**  `masurVeech` is now one line — `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant_perm`, the
measure form the Rauzy–Veech induction proves — and the thirty-line upgrade to uniform Birkhoff
convergence that it used to carry is gone with it: that is Theorem 2's job, on the other side of
the new definition.  `irreducible_case` (Theorem 2.6) calls
`IETFree.UniformConvergence.exists_uniform_birkhoff`; `BlockGood`, `ae_blockGood_free` and
`exists_word_trivial_of_region` are untouched, since they only see the notion, and the notion is
now the weak one they were proved for.  `Basic.lean` keeps `IsRigidByTranslations` (Definition
2.2).

still `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; `Comparator/Check.lean` accepts the pair on 30 899
