# Part II — the Masur–Veech campaigns (verbatim records, blueprints and graphs)

The two campaigns were carried out in a **separate Lake project** at the repository root, beside
`IET2/`.  It was deleted at the owner's instruction on 2 November; what it left is the prose below and
the library in `IETFree/`.  Four things it produced, and where their Lean content sits now:

| campaign | where the Lean lives now | produces |
|---|---|---|
| Rauzy–Veech induction and richness of the greedy path | `IETFree/RauzyVeech/` | the induction both campaigns below run on |
| Veech's rigidity | `IETFree/Rigidity/` | `veecheRigidityFun` |
| Masur–Veech in Birkhoff form | `IETFree/UniformConvergence/` | `masurVeechFun` |
| Masur–Veech in measure form (assembly) | `IETFree/{Assembly, Basic, MainComponents, MainTheorem}.lean` | `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant` |

The sources were copied from that project's library into `IETFree/`, the namespaces renamed to match
the directories, the three verbatim copies of the single-exchange API deleted, and the whole library
pruned to the dependency closure of `main` (Part I, Addenda 150–154).  What follows is the campaigns'
prose, with the path edit described above and otherwise unedited.  Each heading names the document;
the documents themselves went with the project.

## II.1 The campaigns' `README.md` — the programme

The research programme's overview: what the two campaigns are, how the tree is laid out, and what
was proved where.  Written before the Rigidity and UniformConvergence campaigns started in earnest.

# Masur–Veech unique ergodicity

Lean 4 formalisation of

> for almost every interval exchange transformation, Lebesgue measure is the only invariant
> probability measure,

following two sources: the survey of J.-C. Yoccoz, *Continued Fraction Algorithms for Interval
Exchange Maps: an Introduction*, for the Rauzy–Veech induction and
the ray criterion, and the distortion appendix of G. Avila, S. Gouëzel and J.-C. Yoccoz,
*Exponential mixing for the Teichmüller flow*, for the graded
induction behind `RichGreedyPath`.

**Status: proved.**  The main theorem `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant` depends on
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` and on nothing else: there is no `sorry`, no custom axiom and
no `native_decide` anywhere in the library; the single axiom check is the `#print axioms` line placed
right after the main theorem in `MainTheorem.lean`, so every build prints it.
It is stated for the two-bijection datum `IETDatum₂`; `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant_perm` is the same
theorem for a single irreducible permutation `π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` and the copied exchange
`mkIET1 lam π h`.

## Build

```sh
lake exe cache get   # once
lake build           # 8776 jobs, ~2 s warm
```

`lakefile.toml` uses a path dependency on `/opt/mathlib` (the prebuilt, read-only Mathlib of this
VM), so nothing outside this directory is written. The project imports **Mathlib only**; it does not
import `IET2/`.

## Layout

The library is split into three directories.

**The root modules — the statement and its assembly.**

| file | contents |
|---|---|
| `Basic.lean` | the datum `IETDatum₂ α n` (two bijections `piTop`, `piBottom : α ≃ Fin n`), `Irreducible`, `toIET` (total), `ofPerm` (the datum of a single permutation), `simplexOn`, `simplexVolumeOn`, `ae_mem_simplexOn`, and `Invariant μ f : μ.map f = μ`, the definition everything is stated with |
| `IET.lean`, `CutSet.lean`, `CutSetMeasure.lean` | the interval-exchange API of `IET2/IETFree`, copied verbatim except for the import lines |
| `MainComponents.lean` | the two hypotheses of the proof, `RichGreedyPath` and `UniformPositivity`, the ray statement `PositiveBlocksRay`, and their assembly `main_of_components` |
| `Assembly.lean` | uniqueness of the invariant probability measure from the ray condition and injectivity of the length map |
| `MainTheorem.lean` | `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant`, its single-permutation form `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant_perm`, and the axiom report (one `#print axioms`, right after the main theorem) |
| `MainCounterexample.lean` | the counterexample that forces the hypothesis `μ (Ico 0 1) = 1` in the statement |

**`RauzyVeech/` — the Rauzy–Veech induction.**  The step and the path matrices (`Step`, `Path`, `RauzyReach`, `RauzyPath`, `PairReach`, `CylinderGrowth`); the volume of path cylinders (`Volume`, `Affine`, `CylinderVolume`, `BalancedSet`, `ChildVolume`); the normalised columns and their spread (`ColDiam`, `PosBlock`, `PosBlocks`, `Peel`, `MeshShrink`, `LengthInjective`); the ray criterion and its inputs (`RayCriterion`, `RayPath`, `RayPointwise`, `ClosureSimplex`, `BoundedSimplex`, `SimplexAe`, `RefiningPartition`, `LevyRecurrence`, `CylinderRecurrence`); the towers and their floors (`TowerLevel`, `TowerLevelN`, `TowerLevelOne`, `TowerCells`, `TowerGlue`, `TowerTiling`, `TowerInjectivity`, `IterGlue`, `IterGlue2`, `TrueStep`, `FirstReturn`, `LevelN`, `Nesting`, `NameInfinite`, `NestedCylinder`).

**`RauzyVeech/RichPath/` — the proof of `RichGreedyPath`.**  The height functionals of a node (`NodeHeight`), the cylinder mass and Kerckhoff's lemma (`CylinderMass`), the stopping bookkeeping (`Stopping`, `BadFirstStop`), the `k → k+1` dichotomy (`HeightDichotomy`), the new-large-letter step (`LargeLetter`), the level masses and the covering bound (`LevelMass`), the minimal exit and the mass of `Γ₂` (`MinimalExit`, `MinimalExitMass`, `MassFunction`, `MassGrowth`), the straddle-mass estimate and the assembly of the induction step (`StraddleMass`, `InductionAssembly`), the `A'`-sum potential that closes `Γ₃` (`Potential`), bounded lag at a balanced node (`BoundedLag`), the graded induction of Theorem A.1 (`GradedInduction`), the reduction to the richness statement (`RichPathAssembly`) and the unconditional proof (`RichGreedyPath`).

`MasurVeech.lean` is the umbrella module: it imports everything and carries a longer description of
the layout.

## Conventions

* **Two bijections.**  `IETDatum₂ α n` records `piTop piBottom : α ≃ Fin n` — the source's
  $(\pi_1,\pi_0)$ — not a single permutation.  The exchange is the copied `mkIET1` applied to
  `π_top ∘ π_bottom⁻¹` and to the lengths in bottom order (`IETDatum₂.toIET_eq_mkIET1`).
* **Lengths are indexed by the alphabet `α`**, so that the step's `λ = V λ̂` is an identity of
  `α`-indexed vectors.
* **`toIET` is total**, with the identity as junk value off the simplex (the `mkIETFun` convention);
  the statement carries **no** hypothesis on `lam`.
* **`simplexVolumeOn α`** is the `(card α - 1)`-dimensional Lebesgue measure on the simplex; it
  depends on the alphabet only, and its independence of the chosen equivalence is
  `simplexVolume_map_perm`.
* The conclusion of `masurVeech_ae_unique_invariant_perm` is **uniqueness of the invariant probability
  measure**.  The stronger **Birkhoff-averages form** — uniform convergence of the averages of every
  continuous test function, which is `MasurVeechFun` in `IET2/ChallengeWeak.lean` — is also proved
  here, as `MasurVeech.UniformConvergence.masurVeechFun`
  (`UniformConvergence/IET.lean`); see `UniformConvergence/BLUEPRINT-1.md` (the compact
  case) and `BLUEPRINT-2.md` (the split-interval model of an exchange), and `UniformConvergence/README.md`.

## What the proof uses

The main theorem is assembled from two statements about the greedy path of a length vector plus the
injectivity of the length map:

* `RichGreedyPath` — a.e. the greedy path of `λ` passes through any prescribed vertex of the diagram
  and then follows any prescribed word, arbitrarily late.  Proved in `RauzyVeech/RichPath/` by the
  graded induction of the source's distortion theorem: the base case and the pigeonhole `Γ₁`, the
  extension step `Γ₂`, Kerckhoff's `Γ₃` (closed here by the `A'`-sum potential) and the new-large-letter
  step `Γ₄`.
* `UniformPositivity` — one constant bounds the entries of a strictly positive Rauzy matrix reachable
  from every admissible vertex (the source's Corollary 4).
* `PositiveBlocksRay` — four lines of measure theory: positive blocks with a fixed entry bound at
  unbounded times give the ray condition, hence unique ergodicity by `Assembly.masurVeech_of_components`.

## II.2.1 The rigidity blueprint

The blueprint of Veech's rigidity: Veech (1984) Theorem 1.4 in the form of `VeechRigidityFun`,
proved from the richness of the Rauzy path, §1–§9.  `IETFree/Rigidity/*.lean` cite its sections by
number, and it is where the gaps of the printed argument are repaired on paper.

# Blueprint: Veech rigidity from richness of the Rauzy path

*Goal of this document: a proof plan, detailed enough to formalise without further thought, of*

> **Veech (1984), Theorem 1.4, in the form needed for `VeechRigidityFun`**:
> for every irreducible interval exchange datum and almost every length vector, the exchange is
> **rigid by translations**, in the strong form where the return times `q` can be taken
> arbitrarily large, jointly with the precision.

*Input used*: only `RichPath.richGreedyPath` (richness of the greedy Rauzy path, proved in
`RauzyVeech/RichPath/`) together with the tower machinery of `RauzyVeech/`.
*Output*: a subdirectory `Rigidity/` whose final theorem has, as its conclusion,
verbatim the `IsRigidByTranslationsFun` of `IET2/ChallengeWeak.lean`, packaged as
`VeechRigidityFun`.

Everything below is stated in the library's own language, with the exact names of the declarations
that are to be used or produced.

---

## 0. Executive summary of the argument

Let `T = P.toIET lam` be an exchange with `lam` typical, and let `γ` be a prefix of the greedy Rauzy
path of `lam`. The *node* at time `|γ|` is the datum `vertex P γ`, with renormalised lengths

  `σ := λ^{(γ)} := Tower.lamAfter P γ lam`   and base length  `Λ := ∑ a, (σ a : ℝ)`.

The induced map of `T` on the base interval `J = [0, Λ)` is the exchange of the node, and `T` is a
tower over `J`: the cell

  `C_b := Tower.cellAt P γ lam b`  (an interval of length `σ_b`)

has height

  `h_b := ∑ a, (Path.Q P γ a b)`   (the `b`-th column sum of the Rauzy matrix),

`T^{h_b}` is the **translation** `x ↦ x + τ_b` on the whole cell `C_b` (`TowerInjectivity.SH_all`),
and the whole tower over `C_b` is `⋃_{i<h_b} T^i(C_b)`, a disjoint union of intervals.

**Veech's idea.** If at some node

  (i) one cell `C_b` occupies a proportion `≥ 1-δ` of the base, and
  (ii) the tower over `C_b` occupies a proportion `≥ 1-δ` of `[0,1)`,

then `q := h_b`, `t := τ_b` and

  `B := ⋃_{i<h_b} T^i(C_b ∩ (C_b - τ_b))`

satisfy `|B| ≥ 1 - O(δ)`, `|t| ≤ O(δ)` and

  `T^q x = x + t`   **exactly**, for every `x ∈ B`.

That is a rigid step, with `q` as large as we like: `Λ → 0` along the path forces `h_b → ∞`.

**How to get (i) and (ii) from richness.** Condition (ii) says that the `b`-th tower dominates the
total mass `∑_c h_c σ_c = 1`; it follows from *comparability of the heights* `h_c`, which in turn
follows as soon as the **last block of the prefix `γ` is a positive matrix with bounded entries**
(Veech's positive block `B`; here `IETDatum₂.exists_uniform_bound'`). Condition (i) is a **cone
condition** on `σ`, and is produced as follows — the only place where the argument departs from
Veech's printed proof:

> fix once and for all a vertex `π₁` at which some letter `b` is *last in the top order and first in
> the bottom order* (such a vertex exists in every Rauzy class: `PairReach.exists_last_true_first`),
> and let the greedy path follow, at `π₁`, `K` consecutive steps of type `true`. Then the
> renormalised vector at the *beginning* of this run belongs, **for every choice of the vector at
> its end**, to the cone `{σ : σ_b > ∑_c v_c σ_c}`; and every vector of this cone satisfies
> `σ_b ≥ (1-δ)Λ` as soon as `v_c ≥ 1/δ` for all `c ≠ b`.

Concretely, the word followed at the pinned vertex is `γ₀ = Bw ++ true^K`, where `Bw` is a
**positive cycle** at `π₁`. Richness gives, for a.e. `λ`, arbitrarily large times `m` with

  `λ ∈ Δ(w ++ Bw ++ true^K)`   and   `vertex P w = π₁`,

and the node used is `γ := w ++ Bw` (**the end of the first part**), where

* the heights are the column sums of `Q(w)·Q(Bw)`, comparable because `Q(Bw)` is positive with
  bounded entries (uniformly in `w`);
* `σ = λ^{(γ)} = Q_{π₁}(true^K)·λ^{(γ ++ true^K)} = (1 + E_{b,v})·λ^{(γ++true^K)}` with
  `v_c ≥ K/(card α - 1)`, whence `σ_b ≥ (1-δ)Λ` by a two-line computation.

So both (i) and (ii) hold *uniformly on the cylinder* `Δ(w ++ Bw ++ true^K)`, which is exactly what
richness can deliver. Note what is **not** used: neither the ergodicity of the Rauzy–Veech map `Φ`
(Veech §3 uses it to hit his set `W`), nor its conservativity. Only `RichGreedyPath`.

---

## 1. Setting and dictionary

### 1.1 The library's objects

Throughout, `α` is a finite type with `[Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]`, `n : ℕ` with `[NeZero n]`,
`P : IETDatum₂ α n` (two bijections `piTop piBottom : α ≃ Fin n`), `P.Irreducible`
(`= IsIrreduciblePerm P.perm`, `perm = piTop * piBottom⁻¹`), and `2 ≤ n`. Fix `lam : α → ℝ≥0` with
`lam ∈ simplexOn α` (`∑ a, lam a = 1`), `lam > 0` everywhere, and `lam` in no stopping set. Write
`T := P.toIET lam : IET 0 1`, whose underlying function is `Tower.exch P.perm (P.lengthsInBottom
lam)` (`TowerInjectivity.coe_toIET`).

For a word `γ : List Bool`:

| object | declaration |
|---|---|
| node reached after `γ` | `IETDatum₂.vertex P γ : IETDatum₂ α n` |
| Rauzy matrix | `IETDatum₂.Path.Q P γ : Matrix α α ℤ` (`Q_cons`, `Q_append`) |
| "`γ` is followed by `lam`" | `TowerTrue.IterOK P lam γ` |
| cylinder | `IETDatum₂.simplexCyl P γ = cone (Q γ) ∩ simplexOn α` |
| renormalised lengths at the node | `σ = Tower.lamAfter P γ lam : α → ℝ≥0` |
| base length | `Λ := ∑ a, (σ a : ℝ)` |
| base interval | `J := Set.Ico 0 Λ` |
| cell of the letter `b` at the node | `C_b := Tower.cellAt P γ lam b`, of length `σ_b` (`CC_eq_Ico`, `floor_Ico`) |
| height of the tower over `b` | `h_b := ∑ a, (Path.Q P γ a b).toNat` |
| exchange of the node | `KK := Tower.exch (vertex P γ).perm ((vertex P γ).lengthsInBottom σ)` |

The three structural facts, all already proved in `RauzyVeech/`:

**(S1) Length renormalisation** (`IterGlue.qApply_lamAfter`, `TowerInjectivity.renorm_apply`): if
`IterOK P lam γ`, then, in coordinates,

  `lam a = ∑ b, (Path.Q P γ a b) · σ b`  for every `a`,  and  `σ > 0`.

**(S2) Tower formula / first return** (`TowerInjectivity.FR_all`, `TowerInjectivity.TL`,
`TowerTrue.tower_formula_level_pathQ_any`): along the greedy path, at every level `k` and letter
`b`, the iterates `T^0(C_b), …, T^{h_b-1}(C_b)` are pairwise disjoint measurable intervals covering
`[0,1)`, each of measure `σ_b`, the map `T^{h_b}` agrees on `C_b` with the exchange `KK` of the
node, and

  `∑ b, h_b · σ_b = 1`.

**(S3) Exact translation on a cell** (`TowerInjectivity.SH_all`): for every `j ≤ h_b` there is a
single `τ ∈ ℝ` with

  `T^j y = y + τ`   for **all** `y ∈ C_b`.

(S3) is the formal counterpart of "`T` is a piecewise translation"; it is what makes the rigidity
statement *exact* rather than approximate (see §5.3 — this is the key point of the whole proof).

### 1.2 Dictionary with Veech, *The metric theory of IETs I*, §2–3

| Veech | here |
|---|---|
| `(λ,π) ∈ Δ_m × Σ_m`, `T(λ,π)` | `P`, `lam`, `P.toIET lam` |
| Rauzy maps `a`, `b` | `IETDatum₂.rvStep true`, `IETDatum₂.rvStep false` |
| `A^{(n)}(λ,π)`, `A(π,c)` | `Path.Q P γ`, `IETDatum₂.rvMat P e` |
| `λ = A^{(n)}λ^{(n)}` (his Lemma 1) | (S1) |
| `λ^{(n)}`, `J_n = [0,|λ^{(n)}|)` | `σ`, `J` |
| column sums `a_j = ∑_i A_{ij}` | `h_b` |
| induced map on `J_n` is `T(λ^{(n)},π^{(n)})` | (S2) |
| `Y = {(σ,π) : σ_m > (1-δ)|σ|}` | `Rigidity.BigCell P γ lam δ b` (§2) |
| `W`, hit infinitely often by ergodicity of `Φ` | replaced by the **run cone** `cone (1 + E_{b,v})` of §4.2, hit by `RichGreedyPath` |
| (3.1) `b_j ≥ ν(B) b_k`, (3.2) `ν(AB) ≤ ν(B)` | the column-sum lemma of §4.3 |
| (3.3)–(3.8), Remark 3.9 | §5 |

The one substantive difference is the replacement of "`Φ^k(λ) ∈ W` for infinitely many `k`"
(ergodicity of `Φ`) by "`λ` follows the fixed word `Bw ++ true^K` at arbitrarily late times"
(richness), together with the observation of §4.2 that a long run of a single type *forces* the big
cell at the beginning of the run.

---

## 2. The statements to be proved

Everything lives in `namespace Rigidity`, in `Rigidity/`.

```lean
/-- The height of the level-`γ` tower over the letter `b`: the column sum of `Q(γ)`. -/
noncomputable def height (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (γ : List Bool) (b : α) : ℕ :=
  ∑ a, (IETDatum₂.Path.Q P γ a b).toNat

/-- The base length at the node `γ`. -/
def baseLen (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (γ : List Bool) (lam : α → ℝ≥0) : ℝ :=
  ∑ a, (Tower.lamAfter P γ lam a : ℝ)

/-- **The cell of the letter `b` is big at the node `γ`**, with relative precision `δ`. -/
def BigCell (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (γ : List Bool) (lam : α → ℝ≥0) (δ : ℝ) (b : α) : Prop :=
  (1 - δ) * baseLen P γ lam ≤ (Tower.lamAfter P γ lam b : ℝ)
```

**(R1) the abstract rigid step** (geometry + towers, §5):

```lean
theorem rigid_step
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {N₀ : ℕ}
    {lam : α → ℝ≥0} (hlam : lam ∈ simplexOn α)
    (hstop : ∀ γ : List Bool, lam ∉ IETDatum₂.cylStop P γ)
    {γ : List Bool} {b : α} {M : ℕ} (hM : 1 < M)
    (hOK : TowerTrue.IterOK P lam γ)
    (hbig : BigCell P γ lam (deltaOf ε M) b)
    (hdom : ∀ c, height P γ c ≤ M * height P γ b)
    (hΛ : baseLen P γ lam ≤ min ε (1 / (2 * N₀ : ℝ))) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (t : ℝ) (B : Set ℝ),
      N₀ ≤ q ∧ |t| ≤ ε ∧ B ⊆ Set.Ico (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ MeasurableSet B ∧
      1 - ε ≤ (volume B).toReal ∧
      ∀ x ∈ B, (⇑(P.toIET lam))^[q] x = x + t
```

with `deltaOf ε M := min (1/4) (ε / (8 * ((M : ℝ) + 2)))` (Appendix A).

**(R2) the Veech statement with arbitrary `N₀`** (§6):

```lean
theorem ae_rigid_step
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolumeOn α), ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ N₀ : ℕ,
      ∃ (q : ℕ) (t : ℝ) (B : Set ℝ),
        N₀ ≤ q ∧ |t| ≤ ε ∧ B ⊆ Set.Ico (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ MeasurableSet B ∧
        1 - ε ≤ (volume B).toReal ∧
        ∀ x ∈ B, (⇑(P.toIET lam))^[q] x = x + t
```

**(R3) rigidity, i.e. `IsRigidByTranslationsFun`** (§7), for the copy of that definition in
`Rigidity/Defs.lean`:

```lean
theorem isRigidByTranslationsFun_of_ae
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolumeOn α), IsRigidByTranslationsFun (⇑(P.toIET lam))
```

**(R4) the target, in the single-permutation form** (§8):

```lean
theorem rigidity_ae_perm {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) [NeZero d]
    (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (hπ : IsIrreduciblePerm π) :
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolume d), IsRigidByTranslationsFun (mkIETFun lam π 0)

theorem veechRigidityFun : VeechRigidityFun
```

`Rigidity/Defs.lean` copies `unitMeas` (`= Assembly.unitMeas`), `IsRigidByTranslationsFun` and
`VeechRigidityFun` **verbatim** from `IET2/ChallengeWeak.lean`, exactly as `IET.lean`
and `Basic.lean` already copy `mkIETFun`, `simplexVolume`, `IsIrreduciblePerm`
verbatim from `IET2/Challenge.lean`. This is what makes the two projects' statements identical
declaration by declaration, which is what the comparator needs.

---

## 3. Step 1 — hitting the fixed word at arbitrarily late times

### 3.1 From membership in a cylinder to the greedy path

```lean
/-- `simplexCyl` is the set of points whose greedy path reads the word. -/
theorem pathWord_of_mem_simplexCyl
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    {lam : α → ℝ≥0} (hN : lam ∉ CylRec.Nbad P) {γ : List Bool}
    (h : lam ∈ IETDatum₂.simplexCyl P γ) :
    IETDatum₂.pathWord P lam γ.length = γ
```

This is `CylRec.mem_cyl_iff_pathWord` (`RauzyVeech/CylinderRecurrence.lean`), read in the direction
needed. `CylRec.Nbad P` is the union of the stopping sets at all words and is null
(`CylRec.measure_Nbad`, or `ae_notMem_cylStop_all` plus `ae_all_iff`), so it can be discarded in
every a.e. statement.

### 3.2 The base shrinks

```lean
/-- For a.e. `lam`, the base length of the greedy path tends to `0`. -/
theorem tendsto_baseLen_pathWord (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolumeOn α),
      Tendsto (fun k => baseLen P (IETDatum₂.pathWord P lam k) lam) atTop (𝓝 0)
```

*Proof.* `IETDatum₂.ae_mem_simplexCyl_nil` and `IETDatum₂.ae_notMem_cylStop_all` give the
hypotheses of `IterGlue2.iterOK_pathWord`; the renormalisation hypothesis of
`MeshShrink.tendsto_total` is `IsRenorm` at every level, which follows from `qApply_lamAfter` and
the positivity in `IterGlue2.iterOK_pathWord`; identify `NestedCylinder.pfx p k` with
`pathWord P lam k` by `IETDatum₂.pfx_pathStep`. ∎

Also record, once and for all, that the base lengths are **monotone** along a nested path
(`TowerInjectivity.LL_step_le`, `sum_LL_le`): `baseLen` at a deeper node is `≤ baseLen` at a
shallower one. This lets a smallness obtained at level `m` be used at the deeper node below.

### 3.3 The hitting lemma

```lean
/-- **Richness, in the form used below.** -/
theorem exists_hit (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (π₁ : IETDatum₂ α n) (hπ₁ : ∃ u, IETDatum₂.vertex P u = π₁)
    (γ₀ : List Bool) {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) :
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolumeOn α), ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ m ≥ N₀, ∃ w : List Bool,
      w.length = m ∧ IETDatum₂.vertex P w = π₁ ∧
        lam ∈ IETDatum₂.simplexCyl P (w ++ γ₀) ∧ baseLen P (w ++ γ₀) lam ≤ η
```

*Proof.* `RichPath.richGreedyPath P hP hn π₁ hπ₁ γ₀` gives, for a.e. `lam`, `∀ k, ∃ m ≥ k, …` with
the first three conjuncts. Intersect with the full-measure set of §3.2: `baseLen
(pathWord P lam ·) lam → 0`, and `baseLen P (pathWord P lam (m + |γ₀|)) lam ≤ baseLen P (pathWord P
lam m) lam` by monotonicity; hence, for large `m`, the last conjunct. Finally
`pathWord_of_mem_simplexCyl` (§3.1) identifies `w` with the greedy word of `lam`. ∎

Two remarks the formalisation must keep in mind:

* richness produces a word `w`; the identification `w = pathWord P lam m` comes from §3.1, which is
  why `CylRec.Nbad` has to be carried along (it is a null set);
* the estimate on `baseLen P (w ++ γ₀) lam` is *not* the same as an estimate on `baseLen P (w ++
  Bw) lam` (the node we use is shorter); use monotonicity of the base length along appending.

---

## 4. Step 2 — the combinatorial package: a positive block followed by a long run

### 4.1 The extreme vertex

```lean
/-- **An extreme vertex is reachable.**  There are a word `w` and a letter `b` such that at
`Q = vertex P w` the letter `b` is last in the top order and first in the bottom order. -/
theorem exists_vertex_last_true_eq_piBottom_zero (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible)
    (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ (Q : IETDatum₂ α n) (w : List Bool),
      IETDatum₂.vertex P w = Q ∧ Q.last true = Q.piBottom.symm 0
```

Immediate from `PairReach.exists_last_true_first` (which gives
`(vertex P w).last true = P.piBottom.symm 0`) and `CylinderGrowth.piBottom_zero_letter`
(`(vertex P w).piBottom.symm 0 = P.piBottom.symm 0`: *the bottom-first letter never moves*).
Put `b := Q.last true = Q.piBottom.symm 0`; then `b` is last in the top order and `Q.piBottom b = 0`,
i.e. first in the bottom order.

This is the classical configuration in which a run of a single Rauzy type sweeps every other letter
through the pivot; it exists in every Rauzy class, and the library already proves the reachability
(`PairReach`, by the descent on the top position of `last false`), so no combinatorics has to be
redone.

### 4.2 The run

```lean
/-- **A `true` block from an extreme vertex is a rank-one perturbation of the identity.** -/
theorem IETDatum₂.Path.Q_replicate_true (Q : IETDatum₂ α n) (hQ : Q.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (hx : Q.last true = Q.piBottom.symm 0) (K : ℕ) :
    ∃ v : α → ℕ, v (Q.last true) = 0 ∧
      IETDatum₂.Path.Q Q (List.replicate K true)
        = 1 + Matrix.of (fun a c => if a = Q.last true then (v c : ℤ) else 0) ∧
      ∀ c, c ≠ Q.last true → K / (Fintype.card α - 1) ≤ v c
```

**Audit fix (m1 of `smvzeyuez`, finding f1).**  The last conjunct is *not* `∀ c, …`: at
`c = Q.last true` the left-hand side is `0`, while `v b = 0 < K/(card α - 1)` as soon as
`K ≥ card α - 1`.  Exactly `c ≠ Q.last true` is used in §4.4 and in Appendix A.

*Proof.* Let `b := Q.last true`, so `Q.piBottom b = 0`.

1. `rvStep_piTop_true` shows that a `true` step does not change the top order; hence
   `PairReach.true_block_piTop` and `PairReach.true_block_last_true` give
   `(vertex Q (List.replicate k true)).last true = b` for every `k`.
2. `rvStep_piBottom_true` shows that in a `true` step the bottom order becomes
   `piBottom.trans (insertEquiv (pivot Q true))`, and `pivot_true` gives
   `pivot Q true = piBottom (last true) = 0`; the coordinate formula is
   `trans_insertEquiv_apply_val` (a letter at position `≤ p` stays, `last false` moves to `p+1`, the
   others move up by one). Writing the bottom order as `(b, a₁, …, a_{n-1})`,
   one step produces `(b, a_{n-1}, a₁, …, a_{n-2})`: the suffix of length `n-1` is right-rotated by
   one. Hence the letters `last false` at the successive vertices are
   `a_{n-1}, a_{n-2}, …, a₁, a_{n-1}, …` — each letter `≠ b` exactly once in every `n-1`
   consecutive steps.  **The count covers only the letters `≠ b`** (audit of `smvzeyuez`/m2): the
   pivot is `0` at every step of the run (`pivot_true` at the first, then
   `rvStep_piBottom_true_apply_le`, which keeps `b` at bottom position `0`), so the suffix of length
   `card α - 1` rotates with no transient and `v c ∈ {K / (card α - 1), K / (card α - 1) + 1}` for
   `c ≠ b` — the integer quotient, never one less — while `v b = 0`.  Formalise this as its own lemma
   ```lean
   theorem last_false_true_block (Q : IETDatum₂ α n) (hx : Q.last true = Q.piBottom.symm 0)
       (K : ℕ) : …
   ```
   or, more economically, count: `PairReach.card_filter_gt`, `card_filter_le`, `card_filter_lt`
   give the cardinalities needed to show that after `k` steps the whole suffix has rotated.
3. `Path.Q_cons` with `rvMat P e = 1 + E_{last e, last (!e)}` (`rvMat`, `rvMat_cast`): a `true` step
   contributes the factor `1 + E_{b, c'}` with `c' = last false ≠ b`. Since
   `E_{b,c} · E_{b,c'} = δ_{c,b} · E_{b,c'} = 0` for `c ≠ b`, the product of the `K` factors is
   `1 + E_{b,v}` with `v c = #{steps i : last false at step i = c}`, and `v b = 0`. ∎

**Consequence (the big cell).** Let `Q` be an extreme vertex, `K` a run length, `b = Q.last true`.
For *any* positive `σ' : α → ℝ` put

  `σ := qApply (Path.Q Q (List.replicate K true)) σ' = σ' + (∑ c, v c · σ' c) · e_b`.

Then `σ c = σ' c > 0` for `c ≠ b` and `σ b = σ' b + ∑ c, v c · σ' c` (audit of `smvzeyuez`/m2: the
summand is `σ'`, and as an equality in `σ` the display was false); since `v c ≥ V` for `c ≠ b` and
`σ' c = σ c` there,

  `σ b ≥ V · ∑_{c ≠ b} σ c`  ⟹  `σ b ≥ V/(1+V) · ∑_c σ c ≥ (1-δ) · ∑_c σ c`

as soon as `V ≥ (1-δ)/δ`. This is Veech's passage from (3.3)–(3.4) to (3.7), with `Y` replaced by a
condition that holds on a whole cone:

```lean
/-- **Big cell from a run.** -/
theorem bigCell_of_mem_cone (Q : IETDatum₂ α n) (hQ : Q.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (hx : Q.last true = Q.piBottom.symm 0) {K : ℕ} {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1)
    (hK : (1 - δ) / δ ≤ (K / (Fintype.card α - 1) : ℕ))
    {σ σ' : α → ℝ} (hpos : ∀ c, 0 < σ' c)
    (hσ : σ = IETDatum₂.qApply (IETDatum₂.Path.Q Q (List.replicate K true)) σ') :
    (1 - δ) * ∑ c, σ c ≤ σ (Q.last true)
```

The passage from this cone statement to `BigCell P (w ++ Bw) lam δ b` is (S1) with the word
`w ++ Bw ++ true^K`: `lam = qApply (Q (w ++ Bw)) σ` and `σ = qApply (Q_{π₁} true^K) σ'`, so
`Path.Q_append` twice and `IterGlue.qApply_lamAfter` give the hypothesis.  The proved form
(`Combinatorics.lean`, deviations D9/D10 of `NOTES.md` Addendum 9) keeps `hδ1 : δ ≤ 1` and
`hpos : ∀ c, 0 < σ' c`; both hold at the point of use — `δ = deltaOf ε M ≤ 1/4`, and strict
positivity of `lamAfter` comes from `lam ∈ Δ(w ++ Bw ++ true^K)` (the cone is over the *positive*
orthant), not from `IterOK`, which does not see `lam > 0` (`hatLam` keeps a zero coordinate at zero).
That is the audit of `smvzeyuez`/m2, R4, in its exact scope: the hypothesis is legitimate, the
*justification* "from `IterOK`" was not.  For `δ ≥ 1` the conclusion is trivial
(`(1-δ)Λ ≤ 0 ≤ σ_b`), so `exists_good_node` case-splits on `δ ≤ 1`.

### 4.3 The positive block and comparability of the heights

```lean
/-- **A positive right factor makes the column sums comparable.** -/
theorem colsum_le_of_one_le (A B : Matrix α α ℤ) (M : ℤ)
    (hA : ∀ a c, 0 ≤ A a c) (h1 : ∀ a c, 1 ≤ B a c) (hM : ∀ a c, B a c ≤ M) :
    ∀ j j', ∑ a, (A * B) a j ≤ M * ∑ a, (A * B) a j'

/-- **A positive cycle at the extreme vertex, with bounded entries.** -/
theorem exists_pos_cycle (Q : IETDatum₂ α n) (hQ : Q.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ (Bw : List Bool) (M : ℤ), 1 < M ∧ IETDatum₂.vertex Q Bw = Q ∧
      ∀ a c, 1 ≤ IETDatum₂.Path.Q Q Bw a c ∧ IETDatum₂.Path.Q Q Bw a c ≤ M
```

*Proof of the first.* `∑ a, (A*B) a j = ∑ a ∑ i, A a i * B i j = ∑ i, (∑ a, A a i) * B i j` by
`Finset.sum_comm`; `B i j ≤ M ≤ M * B i j'` because `1 ≤ B i j'`; sum over `i`. ∎

*Proof of the second.* `IETDatum₂.exists_uniform_bound' hn` (`= Path.exists_uniform_bound`,
discharged by `PairReach`, `CylinderGrowth.exists_pos_word`) gives, at `Q`, a word `v` with
`1 ≤ Q Q v a c ≤ C₁` for all `a c`, landing at `Q' := vertex Q v`. `RauzyReach.reach_back` (strong
connectivity, proved from injectivity of `rvStep`) gives `ρ` with `vertex Q' ρ = Q`. Then
`Bw := v ++ ρ` is a cycle at `Q`, and `Q Q Bw = Q Q v * Q Q' ρ ≥ 1` entrywise, because every column
of `Q Q' ρ` has a nonzero entry (`CylinderGrowth.one_le_Q_diag`) and every entry of `Q Q v` is
`≥ 1`. For the upper bound take

  `M := max 2 ( (card α) · ⌈C₁⌉₊ · max { Q Q' ρ' a c : Q' reachable from Q, |ρ'| ≤ L } )`

where `⌈C₁⌉₊` is a natural number `≥ C₁` and `L` is the diameter bound of
`RauzyReach.exists_path_between` — a maximum over the finitely many words of length `≤ L` at the
finitely many reachable vertices, hence well defined.  The factor `card α` is needed (audit of
`smvzeyuez`/m2, R3): the `(a,c)` entry of `Q v · Q ρ` is a sum of `card α` terms, each `≤ C₁ · max`.
The landed `Matrix.lean` does not use this formula — it caps `M` by an explicit supremum over all
words of length `≤ L`, so the campaign's `M` is even larger and nothing depends on the correction. ∎

**Comparability of the heights at the node `w ++ Bw`.** By `Path.Q_append`,
`Path.Q P (w ++ Bw) = Path.Q P w * Path.Q π₁ Bw`, and `Path.Q w` is nonnegative (`Q_nonneg`), so
§4.3 gives

  `height P (w ++ Bw) c ≤ M * height P (w ++ Bw) b`   for all `c`.

This is *uniform in `w`* — the content of Veech's (3.1)+(3.2), and the reason for putting the
positive block at the **end** of the prefix.

### 4.4 The good node

```lean
/-- **The good node.**  For every `δ > 0` there are a vertex `π₁` reachable from `P`, a positive
cycle `Bw` at `π₁`, a letter `b` and a constant `M`, such that for every `w` with
`vertex P w = π₁`, at the node `γ = w ++ Bw`, and for every `lam` whose greedy path reads
`w ++ Bw ++ true^K`:
  (i)  the `b`-cell is big with precision `δ`,
  (ii) the heights are comparable with constant `M`. -/
theorem exists_good_node (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ (π₁ : IETDatum₂ α n) (_hπ₁ : ∃ u, IETDatum₂.vertex P u = π₁)
      (Bw : List Bool) (b : α) (K : ℕ) (M : ℕ),
      1 < M ∧ IETDatum₂.vertex π₁ Bw = π₁ ∧
      (∀ a c, 1 ≤ IETDatum₂.Path.Q π₁ Bw a c ∧ IETDatum₂.Path.Q π₁ Bw a c ≤ M) ∧
      b = π₁.piBottom.symm 0 ∧ π₁.last true = b ∧
      ∀ (w : List Bool), IETDatum₂.vertex P w = π₁ →
      ∀ {lam : α → ℝ≥0}, TowerTrue.IterOK P lam (w ++ Bw ++ List.replicate K true) →
        BigCell P (w ++ Bw) lam δ b ∧
        ∀ c, height P (w ++ Bw) c ≤ M * height P (w ++ Bw) b
```

**Audit fix (audit B, `smvzhygum`, finding F1).** The hypothesis of the block above is
`TowerTrue.IterOK P lam (w ++ Bw ++ true^K)`; the landed theorem (`Rigidity/Node.lean:152`) takes the
strictly stronger `lam ∈ P.simplexCyl (w ++ Bw ++ true^K)`.  The two are **not** equivalent: cylinder
membership gives `IterOK` through the Rauzy type rule (`iterOK_of_mem_simplexCyl`), not conversely —
on the two-letter extreme vertex, `lam = (0,1)` satisfies `IterOK` at `[true]` and lies in no
cylinder, since a cylinder is the cone over the *open* orthant and its points have strictly positive
coordinates (compiled probe `ProbeD.lean`, `smvzhygum/m1`).  The stronger hypothesis is what *(i)*
needs: `bigCell_of_mem_cone` requires `σ' > 0` at the end of the run, and `IterOK` alone keeps a
vanishing coordinate at zero.  So the formalised theorem is strictly weaker than the block above.
Nothing downstream weakens: the use site (§6) has cylinder membership.  Read the block with
`lam ∈ Δ(w ++ Bw ++ true^K)` in place of `IterOK …`.

*Proof.* Take `π₁` and `b` from §4.1 applied to `P` (so `π₁` is reachable from `P`, `b` is the
bottom-first letter and `π₁.last true = b`), the positive cycle `Bw` and the constant `M` from
§4.3, and `K := ⌈(1-δ)/δ⌉₊ * (card α - 1)`.

*(i)* `IterOK` restricted to a prefix (`IterOK`'s inductive definition) gives `IterOK P lam
(w ++ Bw)`; (S1) with the word `w ++ Bw ++ true^K` gives `σ = qApply (Q π₁ true^K) σ'` with
`σ' = λ^{(w++Bw++true^K)} > 0`; §4.2 with `V = K/(card α - 1) ≥ (1-δ)/δ` concludes.

*(ii)* §4.3 with `A := Path.Q P w` and `B := Path.Q π₁ Bw`. ∎

**Remark (the `γ γ'` of the request).** The word `γ₀` is `γ` followed by `γ'` with

* `γ = Bw` — the **first part**: a positive block at the extreme vertex. Richness pins the vertex
  *before* it (to `π₁`) and then follows `γ γ'`; the node we use is `w ++ Bw`, i.e. **the end of the
  first part**;
* `γ' = true^K` — the **second part**: a long run of a single Rauzy type.

At the end of the first part, i.e. at the node `w ++ Bw`: one coordinate of the renormalised vector
is `≥ 1-δ` of the total (the "one interval occupies a proportion close to 1" of Veech), and the
heights — the multiplicities of the visits of the original cells, `Q(w ++ Bw) a b` — are all within
a factor `M`, uniformly in the (arbitrary) prefix `w` (the "the intervals appear at previous steps
at similar frequencies"). Both properties are *consequences of the two parts of the path*, and
neither is available for `γ` alone or for `γ'` alone: the big coordinate is forced by the run that
*follows* it, and the comparability of the frequencies is forced by the positive block that
*precedes* it. This is why the two must be adjacent, with the positive block first.

Note also that `K` — hence the length of the second part — depends only on `δ` and `card α`, never on
`λ`: the word `γ₀` is fixed once and for all, which is what richness requires.

## 5. Step 3 — from a good node to a rigid step

Hypotheses of §5: `P`, `lam ∈ simplexOn α`, `IterOK P lam γ`, and at the node `γ`:
`σ := lamAfter P γ lam`, `Λ := ∑ σ`, `h_b := height P γ b`, `C_b := Tower.cellAt P γ lam b`,
`T := P.toIET lam`, plus `BigCell` (i) with `δ`, the height domination (ii) with `M`, and `Λ`
small.

### 5.1 Plumbing

Take the nested sequence to be the **prefixes of `γ` itself**: `γ_k := γ.take k`,
`p k := γ[k]`.  Then `γ_k ++ [p k] = γ_{k+1}` (`List.take_succ_cons`), `γ_{|γ|} = γ`, and
`IterOK P lam γ_k` for every `k ≤ |γ|` by induction on `IterOK` — its definition is
`IterOK P lam (e :: es) = StepOK P lam e ∧ IterOK (P.rvStep e) (hatLam P e lam) es`, so a prefix
keeps the first component and shortens the second; no positivity of `lam` is used.  (Audit fix R1 of
`smvzeyuez`/m1: the blueprint cited `IterGlue2.iterOK_pathWord`, which needs `lam ∈ Δ[]`, i.e.
`∀ a, 0 < lam a` — *not* a hypothesis of §5, since `simplexOn` allows zero coordinates and
`cylStop ⊆ simplexCyl` makes `hstop` vacuous on the boundary.  `hOK` alone suffices.)  Then `TowerStep.VV/LL/CC/HH/KK` at level `k = |γ|` are
`vertex P γ`, `lamAfter`, `cellAt`, `height` and the node exchange, and (S2), (S3) apply verbatim
(`FR_all`, `SH_all`, `TL`, `floors_disjoint`, `floor_Ico`, `mem_floors_iff`, `floor_subset_one`,
`measurableSet_floor`).

### 5.2 The translation and its size

By (S2), `T^{h_b}` agrees on `C_b` with the node exchange `KK`; explicitly,

  `T^{h_b} y = y + translationVector (vertex P γ).perm σ' (piBottom b)`   for `y ∈ C_b`,

where `σ'` are the node lengths in bottom order (`Tower.exch_of_mem`, `idx_eq`). Since
`leftEnd ≤ Λ - σ_b` (`upperEnd_le_total`) and `imageLeft ≤ Λ - σ_b` (`imageLeft_add_le_total`):

```lean
theorem abs_translation_le (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    {lam : α → ℝ≥0} (hlam : lam ∈ simplexOn α)
    (hstop : ∀ γ : List Bool, lam ∉ IETDatum₂.cylStop P γ)
    {γ : List Bool} {b : α} (hOK : TowerTrue.IterOK P lam γ) :
    ∃ τ : ℝ, (∀ y ∈ Tower.cellAt P γ lam b, (⇑(P.toIET lam))^[height P γ b] y = y + τ) ∧
      |τ| ≤ baseLen P γ lam - (Tower.lamAfter P γ lam b : ℝ)
```

(the hypotheses `hlam`, `hstop`, `hOK` are only there so that `γ` is a level of the greedy path and
`FR_all` applies; the statement itself is about the single word `γ`.)

With (i) (`σ_b ≥ (1-δ)Λ`) this gives `|τ| ≤ δ Λ ≤ δ ε`: **Veech's (iv)**, quantitatively.

### 5.3 The rigid set, and exactness

Let `C_b = Set.Ico u v` with `v - u = σ_b` (`CC_eq_Ico`, `floor_Ico`) and put

  `E := {y ∈ C_b : y + τ ∈ C_b}`  (`= Set.Ico (max u (u - τ)) (min v (v - τ))`),
  `B := ⋃ i ∈ Finset.range h_b, T^[i] '' E`.

Then:

* `E` is an interval and `|E| ≥ σ_b - |τ|` (elementwise computation with `Set.Ico`);
* the sets `T^i(C_b)`, `i < h_b`, are pairwise disjoint (`floors_disjoint`, `sigma_disjoint`), so
  the union defining `B` is disjoint and `|B| = h_b · |E|` (each `T^i` preserves Lebesgue measure
  and maps into `[0,1)`: `Assembly.invariant_unitMeas`, `TowerInjectivity.floor_subset_one`);
* `B ⊆ [0,1)` (`floor_subset_one`) and `B` is measurable (`measurableSet_floor` and a finite union).

**Exactness.** Let `x ∈ B`, say `x = T^i y` with `y ∈ E` and `i < h_b`. Then `y ∈ C_b` and
`y + τ ∈ C_b`, and by (S3) applied to the single cell `C_b`, with one and the same `ρ` for all its
points,

  `T^i y = y + ρ`  and  `T^i (y + τ) = (y + τ) + ρ`   (`ρ` = the constant of (S3) at `j = i ≤ h_b`),

whence

  `T^{h_b} x = T^{h_b + i} y = T^i (T^{h_b} y) = T^i (y + τ) = (y + τ) + ρ = (y + ρ) + τ = x + τ`.

This is the **one place where (S3) is indispensable**: without `T^i` being a translation on the
whole cell, only the approximate statement of Veech's Remark 3.9 would be available, and
`IsRigidByTranslationsFun` asks for an exact one.

```lean
/-- **The rigid set of a good node.** -/
theorem exists_rigid_set
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    {lam : α → ℝ≥0} (hlam : lam ∈ simplexOn α)
    (hstop : ∀ γ : List Bool, lam ∉ IETDatum₂.cylStop P γ)
    {γ : List Bool} {b : α} {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1/4)
    (hOK : TowerTrue.IterOK P lam γ) (hbig : BigCell P γ lam δ b) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (t : ℝ) (B : Set ℝ),
      q = height P γ b ∧ B ⊆ Set.Ico (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ MeasurableSet B ∧
      (1 - 2 * δ) * baseLen P γ lam * (height P γ b : ℝ) ≤ (volume B).toReal ∧
      |t| ≤ δ * baseLen P γ lam ∧
      ∀ x ∈ B, (⇑(P.toIET lam))^[q] x = x + t
```

The factor `(1 - 2δ)` is exactly `2σ_b - Λ ≥ (1-2δ)Λ`; the passage from this inequality to
`|B| ≥ 1-ε` needs the tower condition (ii) and is done in `rigid_step` (§5.4).

### 5.4 The mass of `B`, and the tower condition

From `|B| = h_b (σ_b - |τ|)` and `|τ| ≤ Λ - σ_b` we get `|B| ≥ h_b (2σ_b - Λ)`. It remains to see
that this is close to `1`. Two steps.

* **The `b`-tower dominates** (uses (i) and (ii)). With `h_c ≤ M h_b` for all `c` and
  `σ_b ≥ (1-δ) Λ`,
  `∑_{c≠b} h_c σ_c ≤ M h_b ∑_{c≠b} σ_c ≤ M h_b δ Λ ≤ M h_b δ σ_b/(1-δ)`,
  so, by (S2) (`∑_c h_c σ_c = 1`), `h_b σ_b ≥ (1-δ)/((1-δ)+Mδ) ≥ 1 - (M+1)δ`, and `h_b Λ ≤
  1/(1-δ)`.
* **The loss from `τ`.** `h_b |τ| ≤ h_b (Λ - σ_b) ≤ δ h_b Λ ≤ δ/(1-δ)`.

Hence `|B| ≥ 1 - (M+1)δ - δ/(1-δ)`, which is Veech's (iii): the tower over `C_b` covers almost
everything.

### 5.5 Two degenerate cases, then the return time goes to infinity

**Audit fix R2 (`smvzeyuez`/m1).**  The constants of §5.4 and of Appendix A are correct on
`0 < ε < 1` and `N₀ ≥ 1`; the frozen anchor quantifies over all `ε > 0` and all `N₀`.  Two remarks
dispose of the rest.

* If `ε ≥ 1`, take `q := N₀`, `t := 0`, `B := ∅`: then `B ⊆ Set.Ico 0 1`, `MeasurableSet ∅`,
  `|0| ≤ ε`, `1 - ε ≤ 0 = (volume ∅).toReal`, and the last conjunct is vacuous.  So assume
  `0 < ε < 1` from here on, which is what makes `δ = deltaOf ε M ≤ ε/(8(M+2)) ≤ 1/(8(M+2))`, hence
  `(M+1)δ < 1/8` and `(M+3)δ ≤ ε(M+3)/(8(M+2)) < ε`.
* If `N₀ = 0` then `1/(2*(0:ℝ)) = 0`, so `hΛ` forces `baseLen P γ lam ≤ 0`, while (S2) (`TL`)
  gives `1 = ∑_c h_c σ_c ≤ (∑_c h_c) · baseLen` with `1 ≤ h_c` (`one_le_Q_diag`), i.e.
  `0 < baseLen`: the hypotheses are contradictory and the case is vacuous.  So assume `N₀ ≥ 1`.

Then, for `0 < ε < 1` and `N₀ ≥ 1`:

`q = h_b = (h_b σ_b)/σ_b ≥ (1 - (M+1)δ)/Λ`. Since `(M+1)δ ≤ 1/8` by the choice of `δ`, requiring
`Λ ≤ 1/(2N₀)` gives `q ≥ 2N₀ · 7/8 ≥ N₀`, while `Λ ≤ ε` gives `|τ| ≤ δΛ ≤ ε`. Both conditions
`Λ ≤ ε` and `Λ ≤ 1/(2N₀)` are eventual in the hitting time, so asking for
`Λ ≤ min ε (1/(2N₀))` in §3.3 costs nothing. Note that `h_b ≥ m` is *not* true in general and must
not be used.

### 5.6 Summing up

```lean
theorem rigid_step (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {N₀ : ℕ}
    {lam : α → ℝ≥0} (hlam : lam ∈ simplexOn α)
    (hstop : ∀ γ : List Bool, lam ∉ IETDatum₂.cylStop P γ)
    {γ : List Bool} {b : α} {M : ℕ} (hM : 1 < M)
    (hOK : TowerTrue.IterOK P lam γ)
    (hbig : BigCell P γ lam (deltaOf ε M) b)
    (hdom : ∀ c, height P γ c ≤ M * height P γ b)
    (hΛ : baseLen P γ lam ≤ min ε (1 / (2 * N₀ : ℝ))) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (t : ℝ) (B : Set ℝ),
      N₀ ≤ q ∧ |t| ≤ ε ∧ B ⊆ Set.Ico (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ MeasurableSet B ∧
      1 - ε ≤ (volume B).toReal ∧
      ∀ x ∈ B, (⇑(P.toIET lam))^[q] x = x + t
```

with `deltaOf ε M := min (1/4) (ε / (8 * ((M : ℝ) + 2)))`; the arithmetic is in Appendix A.

---

## 6. Step 4 — the Veech statement (R2)

```lean
theorem ae_rigid_step (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolumeOn α), ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ q t B, … (as in (R2))
```

*Proof.* Fix `ε > 0` and `N₀`. Put `δ := deltaOf ε M` and let
`(π₁, hπ₁, Bw, b, K, M) := exists_good_node P hP hn (δ := δ)` (§4.4). Apply §3.3 to `π₁`, `hπ₁`,
`γ₀ := Bw ++ List.replicate K true` and `η := min ε (1/(2N₀))`: for a.e. `lam` there is `m ≥ N₀`
with `lam ∈ Δ(w ++ Bw ++ true^K)`, `vertex P w = π₁` and
`baseLen P (w ++ Bw ++ true^K) lam ≤ η`. Put `γ := w ++ Bw`. Then:

* `IterOK P lam γ`: restrict the `IterOK` of the longer word;
* `BigCell P γ lam δ b` and the height domination: §4.4;
* `baseLen P γ lam ≤ η`: monotonicity of the base length (§3.2);
* conclude with §5.6.

All a.e. statements are over the single `lam`, and the whole conclusion is proved for a.e. `lam`
simultaneously — no measurability of the choice of `(q, t, B)` is needed. ∎

**Audit fix (audit B, `smvzhygum`, finding F2).** Two defects of the proof above; both are repaired
in the formalisation and neither changes the theorem.  (a) "Put `δ := deltaOf ε M` and let
`(…, M) := exists_good_node … (δ := δ)`" is **circular**: §4.4 returns `M` *after* `δ`.  The proof
hoists `M`: the vertex, the cycle, the node and `M` depend only on `P` (the uniform form
`exists_good_node_uniform`, `Rigidity/Veech.lean:170`), and only the run length `K` depends on `δ`.
(b) "`baseLen P γ lam ≤ η`: monotonicity of the base length" runs the **wrong way**: what the hit
gives is the bound at the *deeper* node `w ++ Bw ++ true^K`, and `baseLen` is *decreasing* along the
word (`baseLen_append_le`), so it says nothing about the shorter `γ = w ++ Bw`.  The formalisation
uses instead the strengthened hitting lemma `ae_exists_hit_base` (`Rigidity/Veech.lean:301`), which
bounds `baseLen` at `w` itself; then `baseLen (w ++ Bw) ≤ baseLen w ≤ η` is monotonicity in the
direction that helps.  With those two repairs the proof is exactly the landed one.

**Remark (Veech's Theorem 1.4, with `N` arbitrarily large).** For fixed `ε`, §6 produces an interval
`J = C_b`, a number `N = h_b ≥ N₀` and a set `B` with: `J, TJ, …, T^{N-1}J` pairwise disjoint
intervals (`floors_disjoint`, `floor_Ico`); `T` a translation on each of them (`SH_all`);
`⋃_{i<N} T^i J ⊇ B` of measure `≥ 1-ε`; `|J ∩ T^N J| ≥ (1 - O(δ))|J|` (this is
`|C_b ∩ (C_b + τ)| ≥ σ_b - |τ|`). The extra content is the *exact* identity on `B` and the freedom
`N ≥ N₀`.

---

## 7. Step 5 — from (R2) to `IsRigidByTranslationsFun` (R3)

```lean
theorem isRigidByTranslationsFun_of_ae (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolumeOn α), IsRigidByTranslationsFun (⇑(P.toIET lam))
```

*Proof.* Work on the full-measure set of (R2), and choose, for each `n : ℕ`, the data of (R2) with
`ε := (n+1)⁻¹` and `N₀ := n` (classical choice). Then:

* `n ≤ q n`, hence `Tendsto q atTop atTop`;
* `|t n| ≤ (n+1)⁻¹`, hence `Tendsto t atTop (𝓝 0)`;
* `B n ⊆ Set.Ico 0 1` and `MeasurableSet (B n)` are part of the conclusion;
* `unitMeas.real (B n) = (volume (B n)).toReal ≥ 1 - (n+1)⁻¹` since `B n ⊆ Set.Ico 0 1`
  (`Assembly.unitMeas = volume.restrict (Ico 0 1)`), hence `Tendsto (fun n => unitMeas.real (B n))
  atTop (𝓝 1)`;
* the translation identity is (R2)'s last conjunct, and `⇑(P.toIET lam)` is the function that
  `IsRigidByTranslationsFun` iterates with `f^[·]`. ∎

---

## 8. Step 6 — from `IETDatum₂` to `VeechRigidityFun` (R4)

### 8.1 Transport along `ofPerm`

For `d ≥ 2` and `π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)` irreducible, put `P := IETDatum₂.ofPerm π`. Then

* `(ofPerm π).Irreducible ↔ IsIrreduciblePerm π` (`ofPerm_irreducible_iff`);
* `simplexVolumeOn (Fin d) = simplexVolume d` (`simplexVolumeOn_fin`);
* for `lam ∈ simplexOn (Fin d)`, `(ofPerm π).toIET lam = mkIET1 lam π ‹_›` (`ofPerm_toIET`),
  whose underlying function is `mkIETFun lam π 0` (`coe_mkIET1`, definitional).

So (R3) for `P = ofPerm π`, transported along `simplexVolumeOn_fin`, gives, for a.e.
`lam ∂(simplexVolume d)`, `IsRigidByTranslationsFun (mkIETFun lam π 0)`. The only care needed is
that `IsRigidByTranslationsFun` is applied to a *function* `ℝ → ℝ`: rewrite
`⇑((ofPerm π).toIET lam) = mkIETFun lam π 0` before applying the definition.

### 8.2 The case `d = 1`

`VeechRigidityFun` has no hypothesis `2 ≤ d`. For `d = 1` every `π : Equiv.Perm (Fin 1)`
satisfies `IsIrreduciblePerm π` (the only `k` is `0`, and `∀ i : Fin 1, i ≤ 0` is true), and
`mkIETFun lam π 0 = id`: on `[0, lam 0)` the translation vector is
`translationVector π lam 0 = imageLeft - leftEnd = 0` because `Fin 1` has a single index, and
outside that interval the function is the identity by construction. So the statement holds with
`q n := n`, `t n := 0`, `B n := Set.Ico 0 1`. No Rauzy theory is involved.

### 8.3 Assembly

```lean
theorem veechRigidityFun : VeechRigidityFun := by
  intro d hd π hπ
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le (Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr (NeZero.ne d)) with h1 | h2
  · -- `d = 1`: rigid with `t = 0`, `B = Ico 0 1`
    …
  · exact rigidity_ae_perm h2 π hπ
```

### 8.4 Where the result is consumed

Nothing in `IET2/` has to change: `IET2/ChallengeWeak.lean` *assumes* `VeechRigidityFun` as a
hypothesis of its `main`, and the definitions it uses (`mkIETFun`, `simplexVolume`,
`IsIrreduciblePerm`, `unitMeas`, `IsRigidByTranslationsFun`, `VeechRigidityFun`) are all copied
verbatim into the pre-merge project. So the deliverable is entirely inside its `Rigidity/`
directory, and discharging the hypothesis in `ChallengeWeak.lean` is a separate, later step (an `IETFree`-side file
importing the statement, or a comparator entry), which this blueprint does not touch.

## 10. Points of care

1. **`IsRigidByTranslationsFun` must be the copy from `ChallengeWeak`.** It is defined for
   `f : ℝ → ℝ` with `f^[·]`, not for an `IET 0 1` with the group power. The two agree as functions,
   but the statements differ syntactically, so prove (R3) for `⇑(P.toIET lam)` and copy the
   definition verbatim into `Rigidity/Defs.lean`.
2. **`unitMeas` vs `volume`.** `B n ⊆ Set.Ico 0 1` is part of the conclusion precisely so that
   `unitMeas.real (B n) = (volume (B n)).toReal`; prove the inclusion before the measure statement.
3. **Two layers: the word, then the greedy path.** All the matrix statements are about the word `w`
   itself (no identification with `pathWord` needed). Only `SH_all`/`FR_all`/`TL` need the nested
   greedy sequence, where `w = pathWord P lam m` comes from §3.1. Keep the layers separate: first
   the node facts for an arbitrary word with `IterOK`, then the instantiation.
4. **`n = 1`.** `RichGreedyPath` and the tower theory require `2 ≤ n`; `VeechRigidityFun` does not
   have that hypothesis, so `d = 1` is handled separately (§8.2). `IsIrreduciblePerm` is *true* in
   `d = 1`, so the case is not vacuous.
5. **`Bw` must be a cycle** at the extreme vertex, and it must be positive. `exists_uniform_bound'`
   gives a positive word but not a cycle; `reach_back` is genuinely used.
6. **`Q(Bw)` needs entries `≥ 1`, not `≥ 0`.** `colsum_le_of_one_le` uses both `1 ≤ B a c` and
   `B a c ≤ M`; get them from `exists_pos_cycle`, not from `Q_nonneg`.
7. **`q` and the choice of `m`.** `q = h_b` grows like `1/Λ`; the condition `q ≥ N₀` is met by
   asking for `Λ ≤ 1/N₀` at the hitting time (§5.5). `h_b ≥ m` is false in general.
8. **Monotonicity of the base length.** `LL_step_le`/`sum_LL_le` give it along a nested sequence;
   for two arbitrary words use `simplexCyl_append_subset` and the cone description.
9. **The stopping sets.** Everything is proved on the full-measure set
   `{lam : ∀ γ, lam ∉ cylStop P γ} ∩ {lam : lam ∈ Δ[]} ∩ {Λ_k → 0}`; introduce it once, in `Hit`,
   and carry it through.

## Appendix A — the constants

Let `d := Fintype.card α` and `M` be the positive integer of §4.3.

Given the target precision `ε ∈ (0,1)` and `N₀ ∈ ℕ`, set

  `δ := min (1/4) (ε / (8 * (M + 2)))`,   `K := ⌈(1-δ)/δ⌉₊ * (d - 1)`,
  `η := min ε (1/(2N₀))`.

All rows below are for `0 < ε < 1` and `N₀ ≥ 1` (the other cases are §5.5, R2), and `M ≥ 2`
because `1 < M` with `M : ℕ`.  At the good node `γ = w ++ Bw`, with `σ`, `Λ`, `h`, `τ`:

| quantity | bound | source |
|---|---|---|
| `σ_b` | `≥ (1-δ)Λ` | §4.2, `v_c ≥ K/(d-1) ≥ (1-δ)/δ` |
| `h_c` | `≤ M h_b` | §4.3 |
| `h_b σ_b` | `≥ 1 - (M+1)δ` | (S2) `∑_c h_c σ_c = 1` + §5.4 |
| `\|τ\|` | `≤ Λ - σ_b ≤ δΛ` | §5.2 |
| `h_b Λ` | `≤ 1/(1-δ) ≤ 2` | `h_b σ_b ≤ 1`, `δ ≤ 1/2` |
| `h_b\|τ\|` | `≤ δ/(1-δ) ≤ 2δ` | the two previous lines |
| `\|B\|` | `≥ (1-2δ)(1-(M+1)δ) ≥ 1 - (M+3)δ ≥ 1 - ε` | §5.3–5.4, `(M+3)δ ≤ 2ε/8` |
| `q` | `≥ (1-(M+1)δ)/Λ ≥ (1-(M+1)δ)·2N₀ ≥ N₀` | §5.5, `η ≤ 1/(2N₀)`, `(M+1)δ ≤ 1/8` |

(All the numerical conditions on `δ` are met because `δ ≤ ε/(8(M+2)) ≤ 1/(8(M+2))` and `M ≥ 1`.)

## Appendix B — numerical sanity check (outside Lean)

`Rigidity/sanity_check.py` (no dependency outside the standard library) redoes, in exact rational
arithmetic, the whole chain §4.1–§5.3 for the reverse datum on `d = 2, 3, 4` letters: it finds an
extreme vertex, a positive cycle `Bw` at it, appends the run, samples `λ` in the cylinder of the
word, and checks the conclusions at the node `γ = w ++ Bw`. Typical output (`δ = 1/20`):

```
d=3: |Bw|=22, |run|=38, b=0, run column v (c ≠ b): [19, 19]
  sigma_b/Lambda=0.9505  tower_b/total=0.7822  |tau|/Lambda=0.050  h_b*|E|=0.7414  exact translation: True
  sigma_b/Lambda=0.9526  tower_b/total=0.8034  |tau|/Lambda=0.047  h_b*|E|=0.7635  exact translation: True
```

* `σ_b/Λ ≈ 1-δ` — the run gives exactly what §4.2 predicts (`v_c = 19 ≥ (1-δ)/δ = 19`), and it
  saturates;
* `|τ|/Λ ≤ δ` — §5.2;
* the tower mass `h_bσ_b` is `0.74`–`0.94` in the samples: it is governed by
  `(1-δ)/((1-δ)+Mδ)`, and the constant `M` of the *random* positive cycle found by the script is
  large (`258` for `d = 3`, `7.6·10^4` for `d = 4`), so the bound is weak there — this is the
  reproduction of the exact inequality, not of the best possible constant; taking the *shortest*
  positive cycle instead (`M ≤ 4` for `d ≤ 4`) gives tower masses `0.92`–`0.97`. In the proof `M` is
  the fixed constant of §4.3, and `δ` is chosen afterwards, so the quality is not an issue;
* `T^{h_b} x = x + τ` **exactly** for every sampled `x ∈ B`, in every dimension — this is the
  assertion of §5.3 that rests on (S3).

The run identity `Q(true^K) = 1 + E_{b,v}` with `v_c ≥ K/(d-1)` was confirmed directly, as was the
presence of an extreme vertex in every Rauzy class for `d ≤ 6` (exhaustively).

---

## Appendix C — what is *not* claimed

* **No rank-one statement.** Veech's (i)–(iii) are a rank-one approximation, and his Corollary 1.5
  (rank one), Theorem 1.3 (simple spectrum, uncountable centraliser) are not obtained here. The
  argument delivers the disjoint-tower and small-translation properties only at the good nodes
  produced by richness, which is all `VeechRigidityFun` needs.
* **No ergodicity of `Φ`.** The blueprint replaces Veech's use of the ergodicity of the
  Rauzy–Veech map by richness of the greedy path — a genuine change of input, since ergodicity of
  `Φ` is not available in the project while `RichGreedyPath` is, and it is exactly why the extra
  run of §4.2 is needed.
* **Nothing about `d = 0`.** `[NeZero d]` excludes it, and `simplexVolume 0` is degenerate anyway.

## 1. Charter

**Goal.** Prove, in `MasurVeech`, the statement `VeechRigidityFun` of `IET2/ChallengeWeak.lean`
(sha256 `60ac6385…a0b82`), i.e. for every `d ≥ 1`, every permutation and a.e. length vector, the
exchange `mkIETFun lam π 0` is rigid by translations — from `RichPath.richGreedyPath` alone.

**Root.** `MasurVeech.Rigidity.veecheRigidityFun : VeechRigidityFun`.

**Mathematical content** (BLUEPRINT.md): Veech's Theorem 1.4 in the "return times arbitrarily large"
form, and its consequence for rigidity. The mechanism is a positive block followed by a long run of
one Rauzy type, which replaces Veech's use of the ergodicity of the Rauzy–Veech map — that is the
only place where the campaign departs from the printed proof, and it is the part an auditor must
attack hardest (BLUEPRINT §4.2, §5.3).

**In scope.** The nine modules of `Rigidity/` (§5), the frozen anchors, the dependency graph, the
guards, the audits, the campaign `README.md`, and the campaign addendum in `IET2/NOTES.md`.

**Out of scope.** Any change to `IET2/` (byte-identical ruling), any change to frozen declarations of
the existing library, `MasurVeechFun` (done separately, `UniformConvergence/`), rank one / simple
spectrum / uncountable centraliser (BLUEPRINT Appendix C), and the discharge of `hVR` inside
`ChallengeWeak.main` (a separate later step, BLUEPRINT §8.4).

**Success criteria.**

1. `#print axioms MasurVeech.Rigidity.veecheRigidityFun` is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`,
   emitted by a build from a *removed* `.lake/build`.
2. `rg 'sorry|admit|axiom|native_decide|set_option|maxHeartbeats|partial|unsafe'` over
   `Rigidity/` returns nothing outside the manifest-allowlisted frozen anchor
   bodies, and those bodies are sealed at the end.
3. `lake build` is 0-error, 0-warning at the `Mathlib`-standard linter set the lakefile enables.
4. The graph linter passes with `--require-reviewed --require-complete-coverage
   --require-initial-lean-status --require-all-reachable --check`.
5. `check_frozen_anchors.py --root . --manifest … --allow-non-module` passes on the final manifest
   (state `SEALED`, `DRAFT_SORRY` count 0).
6. Statement fidelity: the `rfl`-probe of §7.4 compiles, and the anchor statements are textually the
   `ChallengeWeak` ones modulo the module prefix.
7. Two independent, refute-first audits on record, with no unresolved blocking finding.

  `lake build`.

## 3. The constitutional surface (for author approval before anything starts)

Two definition files and three theorem anchors. All of it below has been elaborated at
`.scratch/rigidity/anchor_probe.lean` (`lake env lean`, exit 0; the only diagnostics are the three
expected `declaration uses sorry` warnings). Namespace `MasurVeech.Rigidity`, matching the
`UniformConvergence` precedent.

### 3.1 A0 — `Rigidity/Defs.lean` (state `SEALED`, no `sorry`, full-file hash)

```lean
import MasurVeech.Basic
import MasurVeech.Assembly
import MasurVeech.RauzyVeech.TrueStep

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal NNReal

namespace MasurVeech.Rigidity

/-- Lebesgue measure on `[0, 1)`, as a probability measure on `ℝ` (verbatim `ChallengeWeak`). -/
noncomputable def unitMeas : Measure ℝ := volume.restrict (Set.Ico (0:ℝ) 1)

/-- Definition 2.2 of the paper, for a self-map of `ℝ` (verbatim `ChallengeWeak`). -/
def IsRigidByTranslationsFun (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ q : ℕ → ℕ, ∃ t : ℕ → ℝ, ∃ B : ℕ → Set ℝ,
    Tendsto q atTop atTop ∧ Tendsto t atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      (∀ n, B n ⊆ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1) ∧ (∀ n, MeasurableSet (B n)) ∧
        Tendsto (fun n => unitMeas.real (B n)) atTop (nhds 1) ∧
          ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ), x ∈ B n → f^[q n] x = x + t n

/-- Veech rigidity (verbatim `ChallengeWeak`). -/
def VeechRigidityFun : Prop :=
  ∀ (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)), IsIrreduciblePerm π →
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolume d), IsRigidByTranslationsFun (mkIETFun lam π 0)

/-- The height of the level-`γ` tower over the letter `b`: a column sum of `Q(γ)`. -/
noncomputable def height {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (γ : List Bool) (b : α) : ℕ :=
  ∑ a, (IETDatum₂.Path.Q P γ a b).toNat

/-- The length of the base interval at the node `γ`. -/
noncomputable def baseLen {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (γ : List Bool) (lam : α → ℝ≥0) : ℝ :=
  ∑ a, (Tower.lamAfter P γ lam a : ℝ)

/-- The cell of the letter `b` is big at the node `γ`, with relative precision `δ`. -/
noncomputable def BigCell {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (γ : List Bool) (lam : α → ℝ≥0) (δ : ℝ) (b : α) : Prop :=
  (1 - δ) * baseLen P γ lam ≤ (Tower.lamAfter P γ lam b : ℝ)

/-- The relative precision, as a function of the target precision and of the comparability
constant of the heights. -/
noncomputable def deltaOf (ε : ℝ) (M : ℕ) : ℝ := min (1/4) (ε / (8 * ((M : ℝ) + 2)))

end MasurVeech.Rigidity
```

`unitMeas` is a fresh copy so that `IsRigidByTranslationsFun` matches `ChallengeWeak` literally; the
probe also checks `unitMeas = Assembly.unitMeas` by `rfl`, so nothing is duplicated semantically.

### 3.2 A1 — `Rigidity/Frozen/VeechRigidity.lean` (`DRAFT_SORRY`, body `by sorry`)

```lean
import MasurVeech.Rigidity.Defs

namespace MasurVeech.Rigidity

/-- **Veech rigidity for almost every interval exchange.** -/
theorem veecheRigidityFun : VeechRigidityFun := by sorry

end MasurVeech.Rigidity
```

### 3.3 A2 — `Rigidity/Frozen/AERigidStep.lean` (`DRAFT_SORRY`) — Veech's Theorem 1.4, `N` arbitrary

```lean
theorem ae_rigid_step {α : Type*} [Fintype α] {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∀ᵐ lam ∂(simplexVolumeOn α), ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ N₀ : ℕ,
      ∃ (q : ℕ) (t : ℝ) (B : Set ℝ),
        N₀ ≤ q ∧ |t| ≤ ε ∧ B ⊆ Set.Ico (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ MeasurableSet B ∧
        1 - ε ≤ (volume B).toReal ∧
        ∀ x ∈ B, (⇑(P.toIET lam))^[q] x = x + t := by sorry
```

### 3.4 A3 — `Rigidity/Frozen/RigidStep.lean` (`DRAFT_SORRY`) — the rigid step (interface of §5)

```lean
theorem rigid_step {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (P : IETDatum₂ α n) (hP : P.Irreducible) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {N₀ : ℕ}
    {lam : α → ℝ≥0} (hlam : lam ∈ simplexOn α)
    (hstop : ∀ γ : List Bool, lam ∉ IETDatum₂.cylStop P γ)
    {γ : List Bool} {b : α} {M : ℕ} (hM : 1 < M)
    (hOK : TowerTrue.IterOK P lam γ)
    (hbig : BigCell P γ lam (deltaOf ε M) b)
    (hdom : ∀ c, height P γ c ≤ M * height P γ b)
    (hΛ : baseLen P γ lam ≤ min ε (1 / (2 * (N₀ : ℝ)))) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (t : ℝ) (B : Set ℝ),
      N₀ ≤ q ∧ |t| ≤ ε ∧ B ⊆ Set.Ico (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ MeasurableSet B ∧
      1 - ε ≤ (volume B).toReal ∧
      ∀ x ∈ B, (⇑(P.toIET lam))^[q] x = x + t := by sorry
```

**Why these three, and no more.** A1 is the target (fixed by `ChallengeWeak`). A2 is the mathematical
statement actually proved (Veech 1.4 improved) — freezing it stops the campaign from quietly
retreating to a weaker a.e. statement. A3 is the only place where hypotheses enter the geometric half;
freezing it makes "`hbig` and `hdom` are *discharged*, not assumed" a checkable fact rather than a
claim. Every other declaration in §5 is an ordinary helper: not frozen, landed only with a complete
proof. `hM : 1 < M` and `hε` are the only non-mathematical binders; `hM` is needed by `colsum`
comparability, `hε` by nothing (kept for symmetry with A2 — **flag for deletion**, see Q7).

### 3.5 Manifest sketch (`Rigidity/frozen-anchors.json`, `granularity: one declaration per file`)

Four entries: `defs_v1` (`SEALED`, `full_file_sha256`), `veeche_rigidity_v1`, `ae_rigid_step_v1`,
`rigid_step_v1` (`DRAFT_SORRY`, `abi_sha256`, `prefix_sha256`, `suffix_sha256`,
`draft_allowlist.frozen_paths` = the three anchor files). Schema: `lean-orchestrator/assets/frozen-anchor-manifest.template.json`.
Honest limitation: `abi_sha256` is "author-controlled" in the skill's schema; we have no separate
authoring tool, so it will be computed by the orchestrator (`sha256` of the elaborated `#print`ed type,
normalised) and recorded as such — the freeze then protects against *drift*, not against a hostile
orchestrator.

## 5. Work packets

Brief template: *goal / ownership / frozen target / allowed inputs / frozen files / checks / stop
condition / hard rules / handoff*, as in the skill. All workers: **write only under your own
`.ultramath/<swarm>/<member>/` directory**, never in the pre-merge project; one Lean process at a time through
the gate (§7.3); no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `set_option`, `maxHeartbeats`,
`partial`, `unsafe`; lines ≤ 100 characters; every public declaration gets a docstring.

| id | module | target declarations | allowed inputs | stop condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PK1** | `Hit.lean` | `pathWord_of_mem_simplexCyl`, `baseLen_mono`, `tendsto_baseLen`, `exists_hit` | `Defs`, `RichPath.RichGreedyPath`, `MeshShrink`, `CylinderRecurrence` | if `CylRec.mem_cyl_iff_pathWord`'s shape cannot give the a.e. form, stop and report |
| **PK2** | `Combinatorics.lean` | `exists_extreme_vertex`, `last_false_true_block`, `Q_true_block`, `bigCell_of_mem_cone` | `Defs`, `PairReach`, `RauzyReach` | if the suffix rotation needs a longer block than `true^K`, stop with the counterexample |
| **PK3** | `Matrix.lean` | `colsum_le`, `exists_pos_cycle` | `Defs`, `CylinderGrowth`, `RauzyReach` | if `exists_uniform_bound'` cannot be composed with `reach_back` (entry bounds), stop |
| **PK4** | `Node.lean` | `exists_good_node` | PK2, PK3 outputs, `Defs` | — |
| **PK5** | `RigidStep.lean` | `exists_translation_le`, `exists_rigid_set`, `tower_mass`, `return_time_grows`, **`rigid_step`** (seal A3) | `Defs`, `TowerTiling`, `TowerInjectivity` | if `SH_all`'s `τ` cannot be identified with the node's `translationVector`, stop |

| **AU1** | audit | refute-first on BLUEPRINT §4.2 and §5.3 against the landed proofs; mutation tests | read-only + own probes | — |

"Seal" means: the orchestrator replaces the anchor's `by sorry` with a ≤3-line, ≤240-byte exact

## 6. Waves, and the agent budget

| wave | agents | packets | why this order |
|---|---|---|---|
| W0 | 0 (orchestrator) | A0 definitions, three anchors, manifest, graph + coverage, guards, gate script | the ABI must exist before any proof is delegated |
| W1 | 3 | PK1, PK2, PK3 | independent given `Defs`: they touch disjoint namespaces and disjoint library areas |
| W2 | 2 | PK4, PK5 | PK4 needs PK2+PK3; PK5 needs only `Defs` + towers, so it runs in parallel |
| W3 | 2 | PK6, AU1 | PK6 needs everything; AU1 can start on §4.2/§5.3 as soon as PK5/PK4 land |
| W4 | 1 | AU2 | final guard and fidelity audit, after the seals |

Total: 8 agents, at most 3 concurrent. If the budget is "4 concurrent, no total cap" (Q1), I would add
a second direction on PK2 (the one packet with real combinatorial risk) and a third audit on the
`d = 1` / transport step.

**Ultramath mechanics.** `ultramath_start` gives every member the *same* task text, so each packet is
its own swarm (1 member), and I judge each submission with `ultramath_verdict` after reading the files
and running the checks myself. Member output is a *candidate*; nothing is landed on a member's word.

## 7. Landing, and the guards

### 7.1 Per landing (orchestrator, alone)

1. `git`-free backup: copy the destination file (if it exists) to `.scratch/rigidity/backup/<ts>/`.
2. Read the candidate file myself (not the report); check the statement against the blueprint and, for
   an anchor, against the frozen bytes.
3. `lake env lean Rigidity/<M>.lean` **and**
   `lake env lean -DautoImplicit=false -DrelaxedAutoImplicit=false -DmaxSynthPendingDepth=3
   -Dweak.linter.mathlibStandardSet=true Rigidity/<M>.lean`.  **Neither is sufficient**:
   `lake env lean` does not apply the lakefile's `leanOptions`, so `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet`
   (hence `style.longLine`, `style.missingEnd`) is silent unless passed explicitly — measured, see
   NOTES Addendum 13, where three long lines and an unclosed namespace got past both checks.  Then
   delete the module's olean, run `lake build MasurVeech.Rigidity.<M>` and **grep for `warning`**;
   a green build is not evidence of warning-freedom.
4. `#print axioms` on every declaration of the module, appended to the file.
5. Copy into `Rigidity/`, add the module to `MasurVeech.lean`,
   run the **one** whole-project `lake build` (expect 8786 + new jobs, warm ≈ seconds).
6. `lake env leanchecker MasurVeech.Rigidity.<M>` (kernel replay; §7.2).
7. Append to `IET2/NOTES.md` (append-only, authoritative) and update the module table of
   the campaign `README.md`.
8. Update the graph (`LEAN_STATUS`, `EDGE:` records as needed) and re-run the graph linter.

### 7.2 Guards

* **Kernel replay** (`leanchecker`), per landing; full replay of every `Rigidity` module before the
  final claim (`leanchecker MasurVeech.Rigidity.<M>` exactly, never a prefix that covers the library).
* **Forbidden constructs**: `rg` with masking of comments/strings, matching anywhere on a line, over
  `sorry|admit|axiom|native_decide|set_option debug|maxHeartbeats|partial|unsafe|run_cmd|elab|macro_rules|addDecl`.
  The only allowlisted `sorry` is the exact `by sorry` body of the three anchors, resolved from the
  manifest — never by glob, and only while the anchor is `DRAFT_SORRY`.
* **Axiom sweep**: `#print axioms` for the root and for each anchor; the root must be
  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; an anchor must report `sorryAx` while draft (this is the
  *positive* check that the draft state is what the manifest says; the probe confirms it does).
* **Frozen-anchor checker**: `python3 .skill/lean-orchestrator/scripts/check_frozen_anchors.py --root . --manifest Rigidity/frozen-anchors.json --allow-non-module`
  (this repository uses no `module` headers, so the legacy flag is the honest setting).
* **Statement fidelity**: (a) textual diff of the §3.1–3.4 code against the landed files;
  (b) the `rfl`-probe `example (f : ℝ → ℝ) : IsRigidByTranslationsFun f = IsRigidByTranslationsFunCW f := rfl`
  where `…CW` is `ChallengeWeak.lean`'s text re-typed verbatim (already compiles, §3);
  (c) `#check @MasurVeech.Rigidity.veecheRigidityFun` printed and compared with the `ChallengeWeak`
  text modulo the module prefix. Recorded as a deviation: `unitMeas` is `Rigidity.unitMeas`, proved
  `rfl`-equal to `Assembly.unitMeas`.
* **Mutation tests** (AU2): for each hypothesis of A2/A3, delete it in a copy and show either that the
  statement becomes false (explicit instance) or that it is not synthesizable from the campaign's
  discharge sites. Each mutation is a permanent test file under the audit's directory.

### 7.3 Machine protocol

* Build of record: `lake build MasurVeech.Rigidity.All` (+ the three `Internal.*` providers while
  they are draft).  Plain `lake build` does **not** reach this directory — its default target is the
  library umbrella, which is deliberately untouched (NOTES Addendum 1).
* Slot gate: `Rigidity/tools/lean-gate.sh` — `flock` on 2 slot files under
  `.scratch/rigidity/slots/`, wrapping a single `lake env lean`/`leanchecker`/`lake build`
  invocation, niced. Workers **must** use it; a build that prints `waiting for a compile slot` is
  expected, not a hang. (Cannot be installed into `/opt/lean`: root-owned.)
* Workers never run `lake build`. Only the orchestrator does, one at a time, niced, after a landing.
* At most 2 concurrent `lean` processes machine-wide, because each costs ≈ 6.8 GB of the 13 GB
  available.
* Record in every brief: one targeted compile at a time, no parallel compiles, no `lake clean`, no
  `lake exe cache get`.

### 7.4 Landing risk: no version control

There are no commits, so an overwritten module cannot be recovered. Therefore: backup before every
overwrite (§7.1 step 1), write through a temporary file in the same directory and rename on success,
and never edit an existing library module in place unless the blueprint says so (the campaign only
*adds* files and appends imports).

## 9. Risk register

| risk | severity | mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| `warn.sorry = false`: a stray `sorry` builds green | **high** | axiom reports + masked `rg` + draft allowlist from the manifest; probe confirms `sorryAx` shows up |
| no commits ⇒ no rollback | high | backup + temp-file-rename; only additive changes |
| memory (2 concurrent Lean) | high | 2-slot `flock` gate; workers never run `lake build` |
| BLUEPRINT §4.2 rotation lemma is the only real combinatorics; if `trans_insertEquiv_apply_val` does not give the suffix rotation cleanly, the run does not give `Q = 1 + E` | medium | PK2 stops and reports; fallback is `exists_true_block`-style block lemmas already in `PairReach` |
| the constant `M` of `exists_pos_cycle` is huge ⇒ `δ` tiny ⇒ weak constants | low | the statement is asymptotic in `δ`; BLUEPRINT Appendix B measures the effect |
| `SH_all`'s `τ` vs the node's `translationVector` (needed for the bound `|τ| ≤ Λ - σ_b`) | medium | PK5's stop condition; fallback: `FR_all` + `exch_of_mem` + `idx_eq` |
| statement drift between A1 and `ChallengeWeak` | medium | `rfl`-probe (§7.2) + textual diff + audit AU2 |
| `d = 1` (`IsIrreduciblePerm` true, exchange = identity) | low | PK6; a 5-line proof |
| the campaign needs a hypothesis that only looks dischargeable | **high** if it happens | A2/A3 are frozen *before* the work; a missing discharge is a `SOURCE_GAP` node, reported, not papered over |

## 10. Questions before I begin

1. **Frozen-anchor profile.** Adopt it as in §3 — three `by sorry` anchors in `Rigidity/Frozen/`,
   quarantined (not imported by `MasurVeech.lean` until sealed), a manifest, and
   `check_frozen_anchors.py --allow-non-module`? Or keep the repository's previous practice (no
   `sorry` anywhere, blueprint as the statement reference, `SPEC.md`-style), losing the anti-drift
   freeze? I recommend the freeze: statement drift is the failure this repository has actually
   suffered, and `VeechRigidityFun` is already an author-fixed statement, so freezing is nearly free.
2. **Agent budget.** Is "up to four at a time, up to eight total" a cap on the whole campaign
   (provers + auditors), or 4 concurrent with no total cap? The `UniformConvergence` campaign left 85
   swarm directories, so I want the number that is actually in force. §6 assumes 8 total.
3. **Compile gate.** `/opt/lean` is root-owned, so the bundled gate cannot be installed. Two options:
   (a) repo-local `flock` wrapper that workers must prefix (my default, no system change); (b) a
   `lean` shim in `~/.local/bin` (shared home: it would throttle **every** project of this VM, and
   `lake build` may bypass it anyway). Which do you want?
4. **Payoff step.** Stop at `veecheRigidityFun` (as planned), or also land, in `MasurVeech`, a
   `main`-analogue with `hVR` discharged (i.e. `ChallengeWeak.main` with only `hMV` assumed)? The
   second needs a new author-approved statement and `IET2/` stays untouched.
5. **A3 and the `hε` binder.** Freeze `rigid_step` as an anchor (my recommendation: yes — it is the
   only place hypotheses enter), and may I delete the unused `hε : 0 < ε` from its binders?
6. **Manifest `approved_by` / `approval_ref`.** What should the manifest record as the authorising
   reference — a `IET2/NOTES.md` addendum number I open for this campaign, or something else? (I will
   not name an author from the repository headers.)
7. **Naming.** Approve §8, or keep the blueprint's working names? Two that change meaningfully are
   `exists_vertex_last_true_eq_piBottom_zero` and `IETDatum₂.Path.Q_replicate_true`.
8. **Scope check on the blueprint's one deviation.** BLUEPRINT §4.2 replaces Veech's ergodicity
   argument by "positive block then a long run". It is verified numerically (§Appendix B) and it makes
   the statement uniform on a cylinder, but it is *my* argument, not the paper's. Do you want an
   independent audit of §4.2 to be a *precondition* of starting the proof work (cheap: one agent, one
   day-equivalent), rather than an end-of-campaign audit?

The campaign's own ledger, 28 addenda: the rulings, the sealed anchors, the audits, the repairs and
the build record.

# The Veech-rigidity campaign — NOTES

**Append-only, and authoritative over anything else written about this campaign.** Read the last two
addenda before touching anything.

The campaign proves

```lean
MasurVeech.Rigidity.veecheRigidityFun : VeechRigidityFun
```

## Addendum 1 — charter, rulings, and the freeze (2026-11-02)

### Rulings of the project owner

1. **Frozen-anchor profile adopted** (three `by sorry` anchors, quarantined, manifest-bound).
2. **Up to four agents at a time, no total cap, no budget limit.** A new agent may be started as soon
   as one returns; no confirmation needed.  (One packet per swarm: `ultramath_start` gives every
   member the *same* task, so distinct packets are distinct swarms.)
3. **Compile gate: repository-local wrapper only.** Never touch files outside the `Rigidity`
   directories, so that nothing of the existing library needs recompiling.
4. **Stop at `veecheRigidityFun`.** Merging the campaign into `IET2/` is a later campaign.
5. **Freeze `rigid_step` as an anchor**; drop its unused `hε` binder.
6. **A new `NOTES.md` for this campaign** (this file).
7. **Naming approved** as in `PLAN.md` §8.
8. **An independent audit of BLUEPRINT §4.2 is to be run now**, and the blueprint amended where a
   flaw is found.

### The three checks, and what they currently print

```sh

python3 Rigidity/tools/check-rigidity.py      # RIGIDITY GUARD OK
lake env lean ../.scratch/rigidity/abi_probe.lean
```

The last one is the transient draft-state probe (it must live outside the guard root, see D4 below);
it prints `sorryAx` for the three anchors, which is the *positive* check that the frozen bodies are in
the state the manifest records.  After sealing, the report must become
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, emitted by `Rigidity/Audit/Check.lean`.

### Measured facts (re-measure; they drift)

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| cores / RAM | 4 / 15 GB (13 available) |
| one `lake env lean`, heavy imports | 9.9 s, RSS **6.8 GB** ⇒ **2 compile slots**, not cores − 1 |
| one `lake env lean`, `TrueStep` imports | 2.9 s, RSS 6.8 GB |
| `leanchecker <module>` | 3.9 s, RSS 6.2 GB |
| `lake build MasurVeech.Rigidity.<M>` (one module) | ≈ 2.4–2.6 s warm |
| toolchain | `/opt/lean` is **root-owned** ⇒ the bundled machine-wide gate cannot be installed (ruling 3: repo-local wrapper) |
| git | initialised, **0 commits, 0 tracked files** ⇒ no worktrees, no diff-based landing, no rollback |
| `lakefile.toml` | `warn.sorry = false` ⇒ a `sorry` builds green; a green build is **not** evidence of no `sorry` |

**Plain `lake build` ignores this directory.** Verified: with a deliberately broken module at
`Rigidity/Internal/TmpBad.lean`, `lake build` (default target `MasurVeech`, i.e. the
library umbrella) still reported `Build completed successfully (8786 jobs)`; only the explicit target
failed.  Hence the build of record is `lake build MasurVeech.Rigidity.All` plus the three providers
while they are draft, and `lake build MasurVeech.Rigidity.All` alone once the anchors are sealed and
imported there.  The `#print axioms` lines of the existing library are unaffected by the campaign.

### Deviations from the approved text of `PLAN.md`

* **D1.** `ae_rigid_step` lost its `[DecidableEq α]` binder: the zero-warning policy, via
  `linter.unusedDecidableInType`, rejected it as unused in the type.  The content is unchanged (the
  binders are weaker, never stronger).
* **D2.** The three source-facing declarations are three one-declaration files
  (`Frozen/UnitMeas.lean`, `Frozen/IsRigid.lean`, `Frozen/VeechRigidityFun.lean`), not one
  `Defs.lean`: the profile requires exactly one top-level declaration per frozen file.
* **D3.** The node vocabulary (`height`, `baseLen`, `BigCell`, `deltaOf`) is **not** a manifest anchor,
  because it is four declarations.  It is pinned instead by `Rigidity/vocabulary.sha256` and checked by
  `Rigidity/tools/check-rigidity.py`.  Consequence, for the auditor: `rigid_step`'s frozen bytes do
  *not* pin the meaning of `BigCell`/`deltaOf`; the audit must check them.  If the vocabulary has to
  change, re-pin the hash and record it here as an addendum.
* **D4.** `draft_allowlist.audit_paths` is empty: the guard forbids a `DRAFT` *provider* module from
  being imported anywhere except by its own anchor, and every importer of an anchor transitively
  imports its provider, so no audit module may import a draft anchor.  The draft-state `sorryAx` check
  is a transient probe outside the guard root; `Rigidity/Audit/Check.lean` is created at seal time.
* **D5.** `abi_sha256` is computed by the orchestrator as the sha256 of the normalised `#check @NAME`
  output (there is no separate authoring tool).  The freeze protects against drift, not against a
  hostile orchestrator; the audits are the counterweight.
* **D6.** While the theorem anchors are draft, `Rigidity/All.lean` imports only the definition anchors;
  the three anchors are added there at seal time.
* **D7.** Ruling 8 is in flight: an independent refute-first audit of BLUEPRINT §4.1–§5 (the
  combinatorial package and the exactness argument) is running; its findings and the resulting
  blueprint amendments will be Addendum 2.

2. `Rigidity/DEPGRAPH.md` + `Rigidity/DEPGRAPH_COVERAGE.md` (24 nodes, §4 of `PLAN.md`), after the

`smvzez5kl` (member `m1`) delivered `Matrix.lean`; **judged by me, not on its word**, and landed as

  `Rigidity/tools/check-rigidity.py` → `RIGIDITY GUARD OK`.

Content: `colsum_le_of_one_le` (Veech's (3.1)–(3.2): a positive right factor makes column sums
comparable within its largest entry) and `exists_pos_cycle` (a positive cycle at every irreducible
vertex, with `M = 1 + 1 + sup` of the entries of `Path.Q Q (v ++ w)` over `|w| ≤ L`, `L` the diameter
bound of `RauzyReach.exists_path_between`).  The uniform upper bound `C₁` of
`exists_uniform_bound'` is *not* used: an explicit cap replaces it, which is better here — it makes
`M` a maximum over a finite set depending on the vertex only, with no length vector in it.

**For the auditor:** the `M` produced is enormous in practice (a maximum over all words of length
`≤ L`), so `δ` in `rigid_step` will be tiny; the statements are asymptotic in `δ`, so this costs
nothing, but do not read the constants in `deltaOf` as realistic.
